pages.wikitext:
{{Marvel Database: Item Template | Title = Iron Man Armor Mark VII | Distinguish1 = Iron Man Armor | Distinguish2 = Iron Man armor (Earth-199999) | Image = Iron Man Armor MK VII (Earth-199999) from Marvel's Iron Man 3 - JARVIS A Second Screen Experience 001.jpg | Name = [[Iron Man Armor (Earth-199999)|Iron Man Armor MK VII]] | Aliases = Mark VII Armor | Model = | Version = MK VII | Reality = Earth-199999 | LeadDesigner = [[Anthony Stark (Earth-199999)|Tony Stark]] | AdditionalDesigners = | PlaceOfCreation = [[Stark Tower]] | PlaceOfDestruction = | Origin = Seventh generation Iron Man armor | Type = Iron Man Armor | Dimensions = | Weight = | Creators = Zak Penn; Joss Whedon; Adi Granov; Phil Saunders | First = Marvel's The Avengers | History = The MK VII armor is the seventh version of Tony Stark's Iron Man armor. It was fabricated at [[Stark Tower]] following several incidents that heavily damaged Stark's [[Iron Man Armor MK VI (Earth-199999)|Mark VI]] armor.{{r|Marvel's The Avengers}} [[File:Anthony Stark (Earth-199999) with Iron Man Armor MK VII (Earth-199999) from Marvel's The Avengers 001.jpg|thumb|left|Suit-up]] Stark used this suit as his main armor, and even used it when he went to have a few drinks with [[James Rhodes (Earth-199999)|Rhodey Rhodes]]. When Tony suffered a panic attack, he used this armor to make J.A.R.V.I.S. check on him quickly. The armor was destroyed along with the original [[Hall of Armor]] when Stark's [[Retreat (Tony Stark's Malibu Mansion)|Malibu Mansion]] was attacked by [[Advanced Idea Mechanics (Earth-199999)|A.I.M.]].{{r|Iron Man 3 (film)}} ==Capabilities== This armor is powered by a miniaturized [[Arc Reactor|arc reactor]], like every previous Iron Man armor. Apparently carrying all the capabilities of the MK VI, the MK VII also has one distinguishing feature that sets it apart: a self-propelled rocket pod form that seeks out the wearer of a matched pair of bracelets, then opens and reforms around the person as a fully functional Iron Man suit. Other notable differences in the Mark VII armor include the following: *Improvement of the hand mounted laser emitters developed for the MK VI. They appear to draw their power directly from the arc reactor, as they are now able to fire continuously in combat. *The flares and forearm missile launcher originally used in the MK III have been re-added. *The shoulders of the MK VII are capable of launching mini air-to-air rockets with apparent homing capabilities. *The legs of the MK VII now store several missiles. [[File:Anthony Stark (Earth-199999) from Marvel's The Avengers 0014.png|thumb|right|]] The Mark VII shows additional thrusters both on the back and the front, hidden under plating. This presumably allows the Mark VII to reach greater speeds, and frees the hand repulsors to be used more frequently and effectively during combat.{{r|Marvel's The Avengers}} ==Alternate Reality Versions==
Image Description Issue
[[File:Anthony Stark (Earth-91119) from Super Hero Squad Online 003.png|150px]] In [[Earth-91119]], The 7th version of the Iron Man Armor was made for [[Anthony Stark (Earth-91119)|Iron Man]] to help his fellow [[Avengers (Earth-91119)|Avengers]] defeat [[Loki Laufeyson (Earth-91119)|Loki]].{{r|Marvel Super Hero Squad Online}} ''[[Marvel Super Hero Squad Online]]''
| CurrentOwner = [[Anthony Stark (Earth-199999)|Anthony Stark]] | PreviousOwners = | Notes = * This suit was designed by Phil Saunders, who previously designed the [[Iron Man Armor MK III (Earth-199999)|MK III]] armor for {{sl|Iron Man (film)}} along with [[Adi Granov]], according to himself, it was the only design of his that made into the film "untouched".[http://philsaunders.blogspot.com/2013/01/remember-avengers.html Phil Saunders' Random Stuff: Remember Avengers?] * This armor has reverted to the circular plastron aperture, rather than the triangular one of the MK VI, due to Joss Whedon's preference for the circle. Whedon has asserted that a circle means something, while a triangle does not. | Trivia = * J.A.R.V.I.S. mentions that the MK VII armor was not yet complete before Tony Stark used it. Given its considerable arsenal, it is unknown what additional functions or improvements would have been made before it was considered finished. Taking into consideration Stark's dismissive command to "skip the spinning rims," it's likely that he considered any additional improvements to be cosmetic only, however.{{r|Marvel's The Avengers}} In later appearances, no upgrades were seen in this suit, possibly because Tony put his efforts in building more suits instead of upgrading his old armors.{{r|Iron Man 3 (film)}} * According to {{ml|Marvel's The Avengers}} executive producer [[Jon Favreau]], the film's scene of [[Anthony Stark (Earth-199999)|Tony Stark]] suiting up on the MK VII while falling off the [[Stark Tower]] was inspired by the cover of {{cl|Iron Man Vol 1 118}}.{{cite web|ref=true|url=https://www.instagram.com/p/DTAlK2MgUxy/|title=officia_bob_layton on Instagram: "#flashbackfriday: Published in January of 1979, Iron Man #118 set the stage for a new era in the series with the introduction of both Jim Rhodes and the Hall of Armor. Plus, the freefall cover inspired the similar event in the 1st Avengers film, according to Jon Favreau."|work=Instagram|first=Bob|last=Layton|date=January 2, 2026|accessdate=January 16, 2026|archiveurl=https://archive.ph/oDTu8|archivedate=January 16, 2026}} | Links = }} {{DEFAULTSORT:Iron Man Armor MK VII (Earth-00000000000000199999)}}

| Title                   = [[Hulkbuster Armor]]

| First                   = Ultimate Spider-Man (animated series) Season 1 22
| Creators                = Man of Action

| History                 = The Hulkbuster was initially created by Tony Stark to be able go up against Hulk should he ever be a threat. The armor can also be used to fight against other heavy hitters.

The Hulkbuster along with some of Iron Man's other armors was being controlled by Doctor Octopus in an attempt to steal the specs for his Arc Reactor. The Hulkbuster was damaged by Iron Man and Spider-Man.{{r|Ultimate Spider-Man (animated series) Season 1 22}}

Some time after Hulk formed his team, Tony Stark created 5 new Hulkbusters, each one was modeled to take on a specific member of the agents of [[Supreme Military Agency of Super Humans (Earth-12041)|S.M.A.S.H.]] in case they got out of control. Leader hijacks the Hulkbusters to attack the Agents of S.M.A.S.H. [[Anthony Stark (Earth-12041)|Iron Man]] comes to their aid and helps to fight the Hulkbusters. Iron Man uses his holograms to fool the Hulkbusters into thinking that they destroyed them. Iron Man showed them footage on the Stealth-Bot infecting a virus in the Hulkbusters armor so that they can be controlled from the outside. Using parts from the defeated Hulkbusters, the Agents of S.M.A.S.H. use them to take on the remaining Hulkbusters. The Hulkbusters then activate magnetizing beams to combine all of them into one giant Hulkbuster as it captures Iron Man and flies off. The Agents of S.M.A.S.H. pursue the giant Hulkbuster where Iron Man states that his [[Arc Reactor]] is being used to power the giant Hulkbuster and use it as a bomb where Iron Man and the Agents of S.M.A.S.H. will be blamed for the city's destruction. After freeing Iron Man, Hulk redirects the defeated Hulkbuster into the river. Iron Man states that he will dismantle the Hulkbusters, but Hulk insists that he keep one Hulkbuster in case he gets out of control.{{r|Hulk and the Agents of S.M.A.S.H. Season 1 3}}

[[Emil Blonsky (Earth-12041)|Abomination]] gains some Hulkbusters that obey his commands after he was pardoned and reinstated into the U.S. Army . Abomination used the Hulkbusters to take over Vista Verde. When the Agents of S.M.A.S.H. return, they end up having to fight Abomination and the Hulkbusters. After the Gamma Hammer that came under Abomination's control is destroyed by Hulk, the rest of the Hulkbusters were destroyed by the rest of S.M.A.S.H.{{r|Hulk and the Agents of S.M.A.S.H. Season 2 7}}

S.H.I.E.L.D. had created Hulkbuster armor based on the Iron Spider armor; it was an experiment designed by [[Curtis Connors (Earth-12041)|Curt Connors]] to defeat very big menaces. It was later used by [[Peter Parker (Earth-12041)|Spider-Man]] to stop the fight between [[Alexander O'Hirn (Earth-12041)|Rhino]] and [[Bruce Banner (Earth-12041)|The Hulk]].{{r|Ultimate Spider-Man (animated series) Season 3 16}}

Tony had created individual Hulkbusters that were each designed for members of the Avengers to use.{{r|Marvel's Avengers Assemble Season 3 8}}{{r|Marvel's Avengers Assemble Season 3 22}}

| CurrentOwner            = [[Anthony Stark (Earth-12041)|Tony Stark]]
| PreviousOwners          = 

| Notes                   = * The Hulkbusters design changes throughout the series
** When first appearing in [[Ultimate Spider-Man (animated series)]], the armor resembles like that of [[Earth-616]].
** Throughout a majority of [[Marvel's Avengers Assemble]] and [[Hulk and the Agents of S.M.A.S.H.]], the armor had a more unique and original design.
** Around the third season of Avengers Assemble, the armor's appearance now resembles that of [[Earth-199999]].

| History                 = The fortieth Iron Man suit created by [[Anthony Stark (Earth-199999)|Tony Stark]] was a hyper velocity suit nicknamed "Shotgun" that can travel in excess speed of Mach 5.<ref>[http://comicbook.com/blog/2013/04/02/iron-man-3-suits-of-armor-revealed-in-detail/ Iron Man 3 Suits Of Armor Revealed In Detail | Comicbook.com]</ref>

[[File:Anthony Stark (Earth-199999) with Iron Man Armor MK XL (Earth-199999) from Iron Man 3 (film) 002.jpg|thumb|left]]
The Shotgun suit responded to Stark's call for reinforcements against [[Aldrich Killian (Earth-199999)|Aldrich Killian]]'s [[Extremis (Virus)|Extremis]]-enhanced soldiers assisting in his fake terror plot against the United States, and was briefly worn by Stark against Killian himself during the battle. The Shotgun's repulsors proved capable of very rapid and versatile firing, even to the point of using a gauntlet repulsor to backhand Killian across the face with highly-amplified force. Killian's counter-attacks tore away pieces of the suit, forcing Stark to expel himself from the suit before Killian finally sliced it in half.{{r|Iron Man 3 (film)}}

==Capabilities==
The MK XL is powered by a miniaturized [[Arc Reactor|arc reactor]]. It has a more aerodynamic design compared to other suits, aiding in high speed flight.

| History                 = The forty-first Iron Man suit created by [[Anthony Stark (Earth-199999)|Tony Stark]] was a Skeleton Suit nicknamed "Bones". It was a black-and-gold lighter version of a full Iron Man suit designed for speed and maneuverability.<ref>[http://comicbook.com/blog/2013/04/02/iron-man-3-suits-of-armor-revealed-in-detail/ Iron Man 3 Suits Of Armor Revealed In Detail | Comicbook.com]</ref>

[[File:Iron Man Armor MK XLI (Earth-199999) from Iron Man 3 (film) 002.jpg|thumb|left]]
The "Skeleton" suit was among those summoned to battle the [[Extremis (Virus)|Extremis]]-enhanced soldiers assisting [[Aldrich Killian (Earth-199999)|Aldrich Killian's]] plan to publicly execute the United States president. It demonstrated the ability to separate into a cluster of separate modules, each rocketing through the air with individual repulsors, and batter an opponent as a swarm before recombining again. 

This armor was destroyed, either by Extremis soldiers or Stark's "Clean Slate" protocol, which blew up the remaining suits to symbolize to [[Virginia Potts (Earth-199999)|Pepper Potts]] that his creations would no longer be a distraction or a priority.{{r|Iron Man 3 (film)}}

==Capabilities==
[[File:Iron Man Armor MK XLI (Earth-199999) from Iron Man 3 (film) 004.jpg|thumb|left|The suit separated into six pieces]]
The MK XLI is powered by a miniaturized [[Arc Reactor|arc reactor]]. This suit is the first in the line of Stark's testing of modular capabilities. It is compromised of six separate pieces (helmet, torso, legs, and arms) that can be self-propelled towards a designated humanoid target and form a suit around the body.{{r|Iron Man 3 (film)}}

The suit doesn't possess the extra layers of armor others do. This and the presence of indentations and open areas in the armor make for interlocking pieces of other suits to fit into place and function seamlessly.{{Marvel Movies|File:Bones kids.jpg|ref=true}}

{{Marvel Database: Item Template | Title = Iron Man Armor Mark XLII | Distinguish1 = Iron Man Armor | Distinguish2 = Iron Man armor (Earth-199999) | Image = Iron Man Armor MK XLII (Earth-199999) from Marvel's Iron Man 3 - JARVIS A Second Screen Experience 001.jpg | Name = [[Iron Man Armor (Earth-199999)|Autonomic Prehensile Propulsion Suit]] | Aliases = * Mark XLII Armor * Bouncing Badass Baby Brother * The Prodigal Son | Model = Iron Man | Version = MK XLII | Reality = Earth-199999 | LeadDesigner = [[Anthony Stark (Earth-199999)|Tony Stark]] | AdditionalDesigners = | PlaceOfCreation = Tony Stark's workshop (Malibu, California) | PlaceOfDestruction = | Origin = Forty-second generation Iron Man armor | Type = Iron Man Armor | Dimensions = | Weight = | Creators = Drew Pearce; Shane Black; Phil Saunders; Ryan Meinerding | First = Iron Man 3 (film) | History = Described as the "badass new baby brother," the XLII saw little action time compared to its '[[Iron Man Armor (Earth-199999)|brothers]]', mainly because it was still in the prototype stage. [[File:Anthony Stark (Earth-199999) testing Iron Man Armor MK XLII (Earth-199999) from Iron Man 3 (film) 001.jpg|thumb|left|270px|Being tested]] Initial tests of the suit were rather chaotic, as Tony had to find the appropriate speed at which the different parts of the body had to travel in order to prevent injury when they assembled on him. Later, while he was creating new technologies in his workshop, Tony tested the suit's ability to be remotely controlled. During his sleep, Tony was having nightmares, and subconsciously summoned the Mark XLII, which awakened and terrified Pepper. [[File:Anthony Stark (Earth-199999) with Iron Man Armor MK XLII (Earth-199999) from Iron Man 3 (film) 003.jpg|thumb|left|200px]] After Stark publicly threatened the Mandarin following the near-death experience of his friend [[Harold Hogan (Earth-199999)|Happy Hogan]] during one of the terrorist's attacks, Stark used the MK XLII to guard his [[Retreat (Tony Stark's Malibu Mansion)|Malibu Mansion]] in case he was attacked. When his residence was in fact under attack by armed helicopters, he commanded this suit to assemble on [[Virginia Potts (Earth-199999)|Pepper Potts]] in order to protect her until she could get to safety. As soon as Potts was outside the collapsing mansion, Tony recalled it to fight the helicopters, but the suit had numerous system failures which prevented him from flying or launching missiles. He managed to dispatch two of the three helicopters, but found himself trapped on the sea floor by debris from his crumbling mansion. J.A.R.V.I.S. detached the suit's right gauntlet to free Tony, and after recombining, the suit, with Tony unconscious inside, burst from sea and proceeded to the next location in Tony's flight plan: Tennessee. [[File:Harley Keener (Earth-199999) and Iron Man Armor MK XLII (Earth-199999) from Iron Man 3 (film) 002.jpg|270px|thumb|right|Harley taking care of MK XLII]] The flight was interrupted when the armor ran out of power; Tony still reached Tennessee, but crashed in a forest. He got himself and the armor to a suburban shed, where he met a young boy named [[Harley Keener (Earth-199999)|Harley]]. Harley helped with acquiring a few sundry items needed to get the functional again, and aided further while Stark made his way to Miami. Stark was caught confronting [[Trevor Slattery (Earth-199999)|Trevor Slattery]], an actor who had portrayed the Mandarin, and imprisoned in a mansion. He summoned the MK XLII, but only one gauntlet and a combined leg assembly appeared, as the rest of the suit was blocked from departing Harley's garage by a locked door. He fought guards for time some with only the two pieces present, and it wasn't until he got the entire suit assembled that he saw one of Killian's men, [[Eric Savin (Earth-199999)|Savin]], flying away from the mansion in the [[War Machine Armor MK II (Earth-199999)|Iron Patriot Armor]] taken from [[James Rhodes (Earth-199999)|Jim Rhodes]]. Low on power, the MK XLII was unable to affect a pursuit however, and Tony resorted to resuming charging it with a car battery found on the property. [[File:Aldrich Killian (Earth-199999) with Iron Man Armor MK XLII (Earth-199999) from Iron Man 3 (film) 001.jpg|thumb|left|Self-destructing]] Once Tony and Rhodes had uncovered [[Aldrich Killian (Earth-199999)|Aldrich Killian]]'s plan to use the Iron Patriot as a Trojan horse to enter Air Force One and kidnap [[Matthew Ellis (Earth-199999)|President Ellis]], he and Rhodes set off to foil the plan. Tony used the telepresence feature of the Mark XLII in an attempt to protect the president aboard Air Force One, but found that [[Matthew Ellis (Earth-199999)|President Ellis]] had already been taken and that Eric Savin was still on board. Tony fought the man, and ultimately killed him with the suit's uni-beam, but the subsequent break-up of the aircraft saw thirteen survivors of Savin's attack sucked out and plummeting to the ground. Stark was able to use the suit to save all thirteen, but the Mark XLII came through the rescue in pieces after he accidentally piloted it into the path of a truck. Stark and Rhodes meanwhile continued their race to a Miami dock where they hoped to stop Killian. During the ensuing battle, the MK XLII responded to the call to gather all remaining Iron Man suits, and finally came to Stark late in the battle when he was fighting Killian. The suit approached Stark in order to suit him up, but collided and fell apart. Stark ensnared his enemy in the collected pieces and triggered the suit's self-destruct, leaving little left of it but a heavily ravaged helmet.{{r|Iron Man 3 (film)}} The MK XLII was later rebuilt, and remained in storage at the [[Stark Tower|Avengers Tower]]. When Stark finished moving to the [[New Avengers Facility]] in Upstate New York, the suit was was one of the many objects and devices left for the final step of the relocation process. [[Adrian Toomes (Earth-199999)|Adrian Toomes]] attempted to hijack the jet that was carrying these items, but [[Peter Parker (Earth-199999)|Spider-Man]]'s intervention prevented him from making off with it or its items, though the airplane crash landed into [[Coney Island]] in the process.{{r|Spider-Man: Homecoming}} ==Capabilities== The MK XLII is comprised of separate pieces, apparently with individual battery units, that can fly to a designated humanoid target and form a suit around such a body. It is controlled from state-of-art chips implanted in Stark's left forearm, allowing him to mentally direct the pieces. Stark commonly uses hand gestures to help guide the modules, although the fully formed suit has also been commanded by Stark's subconscious during REM sleep. When the pieces latch onto a target body, the solid plates extend articulated pieces that reach out to latch with the adjoining component piece; for example a rerebrace and gauntlet will jointly create the elbow connection between them. This gives the Iron Man Mark XLII a level of adaptability previously not seen in an Iron Man suit, and could form around a slim female form with no loss of articulation. The fifteen modular pieces that comprise the Mark XLII are: * Backplate, with attached Helmet * Brestplate * Gauntlets (x2) * Cuisses (x2) * Codpiece * Loin guard * Rerebraces (x2) * Pauldrons * Sollerets/Sabatons, with attached greaves (x2) * Tail guard * Faceplate MK XLII features common weaponry for Iron Man, including repulsor rays, unibeam, flash grenades, and an array of missiles with a targeting system run by J.A.R.V.I.S. A Head-Up Display includes the A.I.'s monitoring capabilities and observational protocol, a Global Positioning System, target scanning, and displays for navigation, power level, and vital signs. The modular power systems ensure that the MK XLII is adaptable, and yet the lack of a constant tie to a central [[Arc Reactor|arc reactor]] also leaves it more vulnerable to power loss than many previous Iron Man suits.{{r|Iron Man 3 (film)}} {{Clear}} ==Alternate Reality Versions==

| History                 = The Iron Man Armor MK XLIII was Tony Stark's forty-third Iron Man suit, and it was the first armor created some time after [[Iron Man 3 (film)|the battle on the ''Norco'']]. It was first seen when the Avengers attacked the Hydra base in [[Sokovia]].

The suit was ultimately replaced by the [[Iron Man Armor MK XLV (Earth-199999)|MK XLV]].{{r|Avengers: Age of Ultron}}

[[File:Anthony Stark (Earth-199999) from Avengers Age of Ultron 002.jpg|thumb|left]]
==Capabilities==
The MK XLIII appears to be a fully finished version of the [[Iron Man Armor MK XLII (Earth-199999)|MK XLII]], it is comprised of separate pieces, apparently with individual battery units, that can fly to a designated humanoid target and form a suit around such a body. It is controlled from state-of-art chips implanted in Stark's left forearm, allowing him to mentally direct the pieces. Stark commonly uses hand gestures to help guide the modules.

When the pieces latch onto a target body, the solid plates extend articulated pieces that reach out to latch with the adjoining component piece; for example a rerebrace and gauntlet will jointly create the elbow connection between them.

*'''Repulsors:''' It can assist Stark during flight operations and provide lift. It can also be used to fire highly-charged and high-density beams.

*'''Infra-Red Scan:''' It is also used in assisting Stark to see behind the walls of the HYDRA Research Base in Sokovia and to locate Loki's Sceptre.

*'''Shoulder Mini-Gun Pod:''' Like other armors, it is also armed with a miniaturized weapons system located below the shoulder plates that can fire twelve shots at a time, six from each shoulder. It is assisted by a computer guiding system to fire at multiple individual enemies.

*'''Anti-Armor Tank Missile:''' The armor is equipped with missiles that is hidden in its forearm gauntlet. It is used to destroy Ultron's body in South Africa.

The MK XLIII serves as a core unit for another Iron Man armor, the [[Iron Man Armor MK XLIV (Earth-199999)|Iron Man MK XLIV (Hulkbuster Armor)]].

| History                 = The Mark XLIV Armor (also known as Hulkbuster) is a heavy-duty exoskeleton add-on to the Mark XLIII, designed for confrontations with [[Bruce Banner (Earth-199999)|Bruce Banner]]'s alter ego, the Hulk. Banner himself helped [[Anthony Stark (Earth-199999)|Tony Stark]] with the armor, which was planned as a "last resort" to control the Hulk.

[[File:Anthony Stark (Earth-199999) from Avengers Age of Ultron 004.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Assembling]]
When the Hulk went on a rampage in South Africa after Banner was psychologically attacked by [[Wanda Maximoff (Earth-199999)|Wanda Maximoff]], Tony was forced to put "Veronica" into action as all other Avengers were either disabled or otherwise occupied. Deployed from a Stark Enterprises satellite in orbit, the re-entry vehicle deployed pieces of the MK XLIV which in turn assembled around Tony's armor. After a drawn-out battle, Tony knocked out the Hulk by tackling him into a skyscraper under construction, and followed up the attack with a hard punch.{{r|Avengers: Age of Ultron}}

The Hulkbuster was later kept in storage in [[Stark Tower|Avengers Tower]]. When Tony sold the tower, the Hulkbuster was loaded onto a cargo plane headed to [[New Avengers Facility|Avengers Compound]], however the plane was intercepted by the [[Adrian Toomes (Earth-199999)|Vulture]] and ended up crashing on [[Coney Island]].{{r|Spider-Man: Homecoming}}

==Capabilities==
'''Modular Technology''': The Hulkbuster suit is deployed from an orbital drop pod called Veronica, that uses its own repulsor thruster to hover in the near vicinity of a commanding Iron Man suit. Veronica then deploys various modules as required, and has spare modules to replace any that are damaged beyond effectiveness. Using independent propulsion systems, each module can fly to the user and assemble into a complete Hulkbuster suit. The inner Iron Man suit is contained entirely within the torso of the Hulkbuster, allowing for the Hulkbuster's limbs to be jettisoned and replaced without harming the wearer. Replacement limb modules are available for different roles, including oversized arms for conventional manipulation, a pile driver arm for high impact battering, and an arm that can open and trap an enemy's arm inside it.

[[File:Anthony Stark (Earth-199999) vs. Robert Bruce Banner (Earth-199999) from Avengers Age of Ultron 001.jpg|thumb|right|270px|Engaging the Hulk]]
'''Enhanced Strength''': The suit was designed to match the incredible strength of the Hulk, being powered by over eleven [[Arc Reactor|arc reactors]] in order to grant the strength required. The suit has enough strength to knock the Hulk about two streets away with one punch.

'''Enhanced Durability''': The armor was built to be much stronger than any previous suits, and to withstand extreme impact damage.

'''Flight''': The Hulkbuster is equipped with repulsors that allow it to fly.

'''Repulsor Beams''': The armor has the ability to shoot repulsor beams strong enough to hold down Hulk.

pages.title: Iron Man Armor MK XLIX (Earth-199999)
pages.wikitext:
{{Marvel Database:Item Template | Image = Iron Man Armor MK XLIX.jpg | Name = Iron Man Armor MK XLIX | Title = [[Iron Man Armor (Earth-199999)|Iron Man Armor MK XLIX]]
Rescue | Aliases = | Model = 49 | Version = 1 | Reality = Earth-199999 | LeadDesigner = [[Anthony Stark (Earth-199999)|Tony Stark]] | AdditionalDesigners = | PlaceOfCreation = | PlaceOfDestruction = | Origin = | Type = Iron Man Armor | Dimensions = | Weight = | Creators = Christopher Markus; Stephen McFeely; Phil Saunders | First = Avengers: Endgame | History = This suit of armor was designed by [[Anthony Stark (Earth-199999)|Tony Stark]] for his fiancée [[Virginia Potts (Earth-199999)|Pepper Potts]] sometime after getting together following a short-lived break up. He conceived it was an anniversary gift for posterity, but Pepper never wore it. When Tony retired following the Blip, the Rescue Armor was kept in storage at the cabin in the woods where Tony and Pepper moved after marrying. The armor remained unused for the following five years. At one point, Tony and Pepper's daughter [[Morgan Stark (Earth-199999)|Morgan]] snuck into Tony's workshop and retrieved the suit's helmet to role-play. After the [[Avengers Compound]] was destroyed by [[Thanos (Earth-TRN734)|Thanos]], Pepper, wearing the Rescue Armor, was one of the many to join the [[Avengers (Earth-199999)|Avengers]] in combat, using various features of the armor to fight both on her own and in tandem with her husband.{{r|Avengers: Endgame}} ==Properties== ===Overview=== The Rescue Armor is the first armor Tony Stark designed specifically for Pepper, though she has worn at least [[Iron Man Armor MK XLII (Earth-199999)|one]] of his other suits in the past.{{r|Avengers: Endgame}} The armor possesses the default capabilities of a regular Iron Man armor, namely increased strength and durability, as well as the ability to fly and shoot [[Glossary:Repulsor|repulsors]]. The most prominent feature of the suit was a pair of drones that comprise an array of modular panels capable of releasing powerful repulsor blasts. The drones could also be brought close together to combine their output into a single, more powerful beam.{{r|Avengers: Endgame}} | CurrentOwner = [[Virginia Potts (Earth-199999)|Pepper Potts]] | PreviousOwners = | Notes = * This suit is an adaptation of the [[Rescue Armor]], and it's ostensibly inspired by the [[Stark Solutions X-51 Stealth Infiltrator Armor|suit]] as it appeared in the animated show ''[[Iron Man: Armored Adventures]]''. * Before the release of ''[[Avengers: Endgame]]'', a suit between MKs [[Iron Man Armor MK XLVII (Earth-199999)|XLVII]] and [[Iron Man Armor MK L (Earth-199999)|MK L]] was unaccounted for, and the numeric designation of the [[Iron Man Armor MK XLVIII (Earth-199999)|Hulkbuster 2.0]] was unknown. Following the release of the movie, merchandise of Rescue showed that the suit sported "0049" painted in the back, and designer [[Phil Saunders]] confirmed that Rescue was indeed the Iron Man Armor MK XLIX.{{cite|ref=true|url=https://www.facebook.com/SaundersCreative/posts/2068754909899757|title=The Art of Phil Saunders|work=Facebook|first=Phil|last=Saunders|date=10 May 2019|accessdate=10 May 2019}} | Trivia = * [[Phil Saunders]]' design for the Rescue Armor was approved after a single sketch. Only the helmet went through a refinement and exploration process, while the rest of the design remained essentially the same.{{cite|ref=true|refname=ArtStation|url=https://www.artstation.com/artwork/W2oKRE|title=Avengers: Endgame (2017) - Rescue Suit Initial Concept Illustration|work=ArtStation|first=Phil|last=Saunders|date=22 November 2019|accessdate=22 November 2019}} * While there was a push to make the Rescue Armor gender-neutral in a similar way to the [[Ironheart Armor]] from the comics, Saunders had a very strong feeling that Rescue needed to be a strong and idealized feminine form in the same way that Iron Man interprets the male form in a mechanical language. Marvel Studios Vice-President Victoria Alonso agreed and championed Saunders' approach. * The suit was initially intended to use red in its color palette like in the comics, ''[[Avengers: Endgame]]'' producers decided to give Rescue her own identity, changing the predominant color to lavender. * Following the debut of this version of the Rescue Armor in ''Avengers: Endgame'', the suit was adapted into the comics as the [[Rescue Armor Model 5]]. | Links = }} [[Category:Rescue Armor]] {{DEFAULTSORT:Iron_Man_Armor_MK_049_(Earth-199999)|noerror}} [[Category:Virginia Potts (Earth-51156)/Items]]

It has a hexagonal-shaped figure around its arc reactor.

[[File:Anthony Stark (Earth-199999) from Avengers Age of Ultron 011.jpg|thumb|left]]

==Capabilities==
*'''Flight:''' The MK XLV, like the other suits, has the ability to fly.

*'''Repulsor Beams:''' The armor has the ability to project repulsor beams strong enough to destroy Ultron's sentries. Combined with [[Thor Odinson (Earth-199999)|Thor]]'s lightning and the Vision's [[Mind Stone]], it helped puncture the [[vibranium]] structure of Ulron himself.

*'''Unibeam:''' The Mark XLV can shoot powerful beam from the chest where the Arc Reactor is placed.

| CurrentOwner            = [[Anthony Stark (Earth-199999)|Tony Stark]]
| PreviousOwners          = 
 
| Notes                   =

| History                 = This suit was created by [[Anthony Stark (Earth-199999)|Tony Stark]] some point after the [[Avengers: Age of Ultron|Battle for Sokovia]], it was first seen being used when he tried to apprehend [[Steven Rogers (Earth-199999)|Captain America]] and other rogue heroes at the Leipzig/Halle Airport in [[Germany]]. During the ensuing battle, the suit suffered minor damage after a miniaturized [[Scott Lang (Earth-199999)|Ant-Man]] got into the suit and began to randomly tear components apart.

The suit was then deployed when Iron Man flew to [[Siberia]] in order to help Captain America and the [[James Buchanan Barnes (Earth-199999)|Winter Soldier]] confront [[Helmut Zemo (Earth-199999)|Helmut Zemo]]. Iron Man turned against his allies when Zemo revealed to him that the Winter Soldier had been responsible for his parents' death in 1991, fueled by rage both because of said discovery and because Captain America had known all along about the Starks' fate but had decided to remain silent. The Winter Soldier damaged the armor's right repulsor, and Captain America busted the suit's right boot, in an attempt at destabilizing Iron Man's flight capabilities.

As the battle escalated, the Winter Soldier attempted to rip off the [[Arc Reactor|arc reactor]] from the armor's chest before being knocked out. Captain America eventually took advantage of said inflicted damage and impaired the suit's power source after hitting it with the side of his shield. He then escaped with the Winter Soldier after leaving Iron Man hindered.{{r|Captain America: Civil War}}

==Capabilities==
'''Rapid Deployment:''' The MK XLVI Iron Man is capable of partial or full deployment onto its wearer at a comparatively high rate when compared to its predecessors. Mounted in a suitable storage receptacle, the deployment can start from a simple finger press of a button, which locks on the associated gauntlet followed by the rest of the Iron Man suit within scant seconds. Once donned, the helmet assembly is also capable of quick retraction and re-engagement, effectively snapping on or off in a second.

'''Repulsors:''' Iron Man's primary mode of attack, and flight part of the flight control and propulsion system, are mounted in the palms of the gauntlets, the soles of the boots, and in the centrally mounted chest aperture.

'''Unibeam:''' Another of the primary features, it is shot from the suit chest's reactor. It is powerful to shoot the Winter Soldier's bionic arm off with a single burst

'''IEM Projectiles:''' It is fired from the forearm is capable of neutralizing the electrical system of an object.

'''Manacle launcher:''' The MK XLVI Iron Man is equipped with a projectile launcher that fires a self-locking shackle that effectively combines the effects of bolas and handcuffs into a single targeted projectile. This system is arm-mounted, and appears to be a single-shot device with the shackles themselves being strong enough to restrain [[Steven Rogers (Earth-199999)|Steven Rogers]].

'''Mini-missile launcher:''' This suit has six mini-missile launchers on each shoulder, along with one on the back of each gauntlet.

pages.wikitext:
{{Marvel Database: Item Template | NoGallery = Yes | Image = Spider-Man Homecoming poster 009 Textless.jpg | Title = [[Iron Man Armor (Earth-199999)|Iron Man Armor]]
Mark XLVII | Name = Iron Man Armor MK XLVII | Aliases = | Model = 1 | Version = MK XLVII | Reality = Earth-199999 | LeadDesigner = [[Anthony Stark (Earth-199999)|Tony Stark]] | AdditionalDesigners = | PlaceOfCreation = | PlaceOfDestruction = | Origin = Forty-seventh generation Iron Man armor | Type = Iron Man Armor | Dimensions = | Weight = | Creators = Jonathan Goldstein; John Francis Daley; Jon Watts; Christopher Ford; Chris McKenna; Erik Sommers; Phil Saunders | First = Spider-Man: Homecoming | History = This armor was built by [[Anthony Stark (Earth-199999)|Tony Stark]] some time after his fallout with [[Steven Rogers (Earth-199999)|Captain America]]. It appeared to be almost entirely similar to the [[Iron Man Armor MK XLVI (Earth-199999)|Iron Man Armor MK XLVI]], aside from the use of two-toned silver painting in the lower torso, upper arms, and upper thighs. When [[Peter Parker (Earth-199999)|Spider-Man]] plummeted into a river tangled in a parachute deployed by his [[Spider-Man's Suit|suit]] following a brief confrontation against the airborne [[Adrian Toomes (Earth-199999)|Adrian Toomes]], Tony had the remotely-controlled MK XLVII rescue him. The suit returned to Stark's base in autopilot mode once Tony disconnected from the armor after scolding Spider-Man and ordering him not to pursue Toomes. When a [[Chitauri]]-based weapon went haywire and split a [[Staten Island]] ferry in two during an ensuing confrontation between Spider-Man and Toomes, Stark flew to the scene equipped with the MK XLVII in order prevent a tragedy. He deployed miniature repulsor thrusters on the sides of the boat and used the armor's laser to crudely weld together the two halves, thus keeping the boat steady long enough until it could be evacuated. He subsequently spoke privately with Spider-Man, and stepped out of his armor to chastise him.{{r|Spider-Man: Homecoming}} | CurrentOwner = [[Anthony Stark (Earth-199999)|Tony Stark]] | PreviousOwners = | Notes = | Trivia = * The design of the MK XLVII is a recolored version of the [[Iron Man Armor MK XLVI (Earth-199999)|MK XLVI]] with a colorway that homages [[Antonio Stark (Earth-1610)|Ultimate Iron Man]]. This is because {{sl|Spider-Man: Homecoming}} production studio {{WP|Columbia Pictures}} didn't have enough visual effects budget for a brand new suit, with the colorway homage being requested by [[Kevin Feige]].{{cite|ref=true|url= https://www.instagram.com/p/CZqIHBFJb1n/|title= Phil Saunders on Instagram: "#ironman Mk XLVII from ...|work= Instagram|first= Phil|last= Saunders|date= 6 February 2022|accessdate= 14 April 2022}} * In the same way in which the MK XLVI is a repainted version of a previous suit with the color scheme of Ultimate Iron Man, toy manufacturer {{WP|Hasbro}} once released an action figure named the [http://marvelousnews.com/database/index.php?itemid=1599 Iron Man Ultimate Armor] as part of their {{sl|Iron Man 2 (film)}} Concept Art series of action figures. This figure was a repaint of the [[Iron Man Armor MK IV (Earth-199999)|Iron Man Armor MK IV]] with the color scheme of Ultimate Iron Man. | Links = }} {{DEFAULTSORT:Iron_Man_Armor_MK_047_(Earth-199999)|noerror}}

{{Marvel Database: Item Template | Image = Iron Man Armor MK XLVIII (Earth-199999).jpg | Name = Iron Man Armor MK XLVIII | Title = [[Iron Man Armor (Earth-199999)|Iron Man Armor Mark XLVIII]]
Hulkbuster 2.0 | Aliases = * Hulkbuster 2.0 * Hulkbuster Mark II{{r|LEGO Marvel Super Heroes 2}} | Model = | Version = 1 | Reality = Earth-199999 | LeadDesigner = [[Anthony Stark (Earth-199999)|Tony Stark]] | AdditionalDesigners = | PlaceOfCreation = | PlaceOfDestruction = | Origin = | Type = Iron Man Armor | Dimensions = | Weight = | Creators = Christopher Markus; Stephen McFeely; Phil Saunders | First = Avengers: Infinity War | Quotation = This isn't gonna be like New York, [[Cull Obsidian (Earth-199999)|pal]]. This suit's [[Avengers: Age of Ultron|already kicked the crap outta the Hulk]]. | Speaker = [[Bruce Banner (Earth-199999)|Bruce Banner]] | QuoteSource = Avengers: Infinity War | History = This upgrade of the [[Iron Man Armor MK XLIV (Earth-199999)|Iron Man Armor MK XLIV]] was one of the three Iron Man suits designed by [[Anthony Stark (Earth-199999)|Tony Stark]] not long after the [[Avengers (Earth-199999)|Avengers]]' [[Captain America: Civil War|civil war]]. The Hulkbuster 2.0 was used by [[Bruce Banner (Earth-199999)|Bruce Banner]] after he experienced difficulty transforming into the Hulk. Banner wore the armor into battle alongside [[T'Challa (Earth-199999)|Black Panther]], [[Steven Rogers (Earth-199999)|Steve Rogers]], [[Okoye (Earth-199999)|Okoye]], [[Wanda Maximoff (Earth-199999)|Scarlet Witch]], [[Natalia Romanoff (Earth-199999)|Black Widow]], and [[James Buchanan Barnes (Earth-199999)|White Wolf]] against the forces of [[Proxima Midnight (Earth-199999)|Proxima Midnight]], [[Corvus Glaive (Earth-199999)|Corvus Glaive]] and [[Cull Obsidian (Earth-199999)|Cull Obsidian]] in Wakanda. During the battle, Banner managed to successfully maneuver in the Hulk-like armor, remarking that it was very similar to actually being the Hulk. He went toe to toe with Cull Obsidian and even blasted the alien into Wakanda's energy barrier, killing him. Throughout the course of the battle, the armor dealt a great amount of damage, but was heavily damaged when [[Thanos (Earth-199999)|Thanos]] used the [[Infinity Stones|Space Stone]] to trap the armor inside a cliff wall in [[Wakanda]] while approaching to collect the [[Mind Stone]] from [[Vision (Earth-199999)|Vision]]'s head.{{r|Avengers: Infinity War}} ==Properties== ===Overview=== The Hulkbuster 2.0 is the successor to the first Hulkbuster Armor, MK XLIV. It is shown to have similar properties, capable of facing off against foes as large as the Hulk or Cull Obsidian. It was also able to hold its own against hundreds of thousands of Outriders for a sustained period of time, though was ultimately overrun and was only saved by the arrival of [[Thor Odinson (Earth-199999)|Thor]], [[Rocket Raccoon (Earth-199999)|Rocket Raccoon]], and [[Groot (Earth-199999)|Groot]]. The armor has the HUD typical of an Iron Man armor and is also assumed to have the onboard A.I. [[F.R.I.D.A.Y. (Earth-199999)|F.R.I.D.A.Y.]] included, though Banner never utilizes it.{{r|Avengers: Infinity War}} ===Offensive Powers=== The armor possesses the default offensive capabilities of a regular Iron Man armor, though generally enhanced in effectiveness, namely increased strength and repulsor rays. The strength enhancement allowed Banner to fully battle powerful foes like Cull Obsidian with matched strength and agility. The armor can fire off more powerful blasts from its hands and also detach limbs via rocket thrusters, which is how Banner managed to launch Cull Obsidian into the Wakandan barrier.{{r|Avengers: Infinity War}} ===Defensive Powers=== In addition to the typical protection provided by an Iron Man armor, the Hulkbuster 2.0 provides the extra defense of the original Hulkbuster armor, allowing the armor to mimic the strength and durability of the Hulk, which allowed Banner to take several hits from different enemies during the Battle of Wakanda. The armor's defensive capabilities held up for a sustained period of time, though the eventual onslaught of Outriders was enough to take it down and damage it.{{r|Avengers: Infinity War}} | CurrentOwner = [[Bruce Banner (Earth-199999)|Bruce Banner]] | PreviousOwners = [[Anthony Stark (Earth-199999)|Tony Stark]] | Notes = * When this armor first debuted, its numeric designation was unknown. Tentatively, it was either MK XLVIII or MK XLIX. For marketing purposes, it was only referred as "Hulkbuster 2.0."By [http://www.sideshowcollectors.com/forums/marvel-action-figures/187895-hot-toys-avengers-infinity-war-1-6th-hulkbuster-2-0-collectible-figure.html Hot Toys], [http://www.bandaionline.com/chogokin-x-s-h-figuarts-hulk-buster-mark-2-0-avengers-infinity-war-action-figure/ Bandai] and ''[[Marvel Future Fight]]'' Following the reveal of the [[Rescue Armor]] from ''[[Avengers: Endgame]]'' as MK XLIX,{{cite|ref=true|url=https://www.facebook.com/SaundersCreative/posts/2068754909899757|title=The Art of Phil Saunders|work=Facebook|first=Phil|last=Saunders|date=10 May 2019|accessdate=10 May 2019}} designer [[Phil Saunders]] confirmed the Hulkbuster 2.0 was in fact MK XLVIII.{{cite|ref=true|url=https://www.facebook.com/SaundersCreative/posts/2068754909899757?comment_id=2068830939892154&reply_comment_id=2069542296487685|title=The Art of Phil Saunders (comment)|work=Facebook|first=Phil|last=Saunders|date=10 May 2019|accessdate=10 May 2019}} * Unlike the original Hulkbuster armor, which serves as an add-on to the [[Iron Man Armor MK XLIII (Earth-199999)|MK XLIII]], the Hulkbuster 2.0 does not require another Iron Man armor to operate, as demonstrated by Bruce Banner. | Trivia = | Links = }} {{DEFAULTSORT:Iron_Man_Armor_MK_048_(Earth-199999)}} [[Category:Anthony Stark (Earth-51156)/Items]]

| History                 = The thirty-third Iron Man suit created by [[Anthony Stark (Earth-199999)|Tony Stark]] was an enhanced energy suit nicknamed "the Silver Centurion". It has a slight protective force field, which allows the suit to attract or repulse objects using its magnetic polarity. The suit is also capable of firing pulse cannons that build in intensity the further they travel.<ref>[http://comicbook.com/blog/2013/04/02/iron-man-3-suits-of-armor-revealed-in-detail/ Iron Man 3 Suits Of Armor Revealed In Detail | Comicbook.com]</ref>

The Silver Centurion suit was among those summoned by Stark to battle [[Extremis (Virus)|Extremis]]-enhanced soldiers assisting [[Aldrich Killian (Earth-199999)|Aldrich Killian]]'s plot. Initially delivered to the battle by Stark's AI program [[J.A.R.V.I.S. (Earth-199999)|J.A.R.V.I.S.]], the Silver Centurion became the first of the Iron Man armor suits that Stark used against the assembled Extremis force.

[[File:Anthony Stark (Earth-199999) with Iron Man Armor MK XXXIII (Earth-199999) from Iron Man 3 (film) 002.jpg|thumb|left]]
When Stark attempted to rescue [[Virginia Potts (Earth-199999)|Pepper Potts]], Killian ripped the front of the Silver Centurion's breastplate out in a surprise attack, before superheating the upper abdominal plating. Stark then unsheathed a hidden blade from a gauntlet to ward off a blow. The heavily damaged Silver Centurion gave him some trouble as it failed to properly release him, forcing him to squirm and kick to get clear of it.

The Silver Centurion was left inoperable on the ground, and it remains unclear whether it was destroyed during the battle, or whether the suit was able to self-destruct later when Stark activated his "Clean Slate" protocol.{{r|Iron Man 3 (film)}}

==Capabilities==
The Iron Man Armor MK XXXIII saves more energy than any other Iron Man suits. It has hidden blades in the arm that can be used in battles.

| History                 = The successor to the [[Iron Man Armor Model 5|Model 5]], this armor was utilized against the [[Kree]] forces during [[Operation Galactic Storm]], notably against [[Roco-Bai (Earth-616)|Shatterax]] and [[Ronan (Earth-616)|Ronan]]. Stark was still suffering to techno-organic parasite created by [[Kearson DeWitt (Earth-616)|Kearson DeWitt]] during this period.{{r|Iron Man Vol 1 278|279}}

The physical stress caused by wearing this armor during the war only made Stark's condition worse.{{r|Iron Man Vol 1 280}}

[[File:Anthony Stark (Earth-616) with Space Armor MK II from Iron Man Vol 1 278 002.jpg|thumb|left]]
==Capabilities==
Various systems were improved over the original. The computer could simulate possible scenarios and gain access to [[Kree]] systems. The armor's cloaking and ECM were enhanced to deal with Shi'ar and Kree starships; however, the cloaking was used sparingly to not further damage Stark. Life support was enhanced and kept a detailed analysis of Stark's nerve damage. In addition to {{Power|Repulsor Ray|repulsors}}, unibeam and concussion beams, this armor had a powerful self-destruct mode.

| History                 = After [[Iron Man Armor Model 9|an earlier armor]] was damaged in battle with the [[Masters of Silence (Earth-616)|Masters of Silence]], Stark donned an armor with more weaponry, which he called the War Machine.{{r|Iron Man Vol 1 281}} It was further modified for [[James Rhodes (Earth-616)|James Rhodes]], who started using this armor alongside his new alias, War Machine.{{r|Iron Man Vol 1 284}}

Rhodey lost this armor after a time-travel adventure,{{r|War Machine Vol 1 17}} and started using and [[Eidolon Warwear|alien armor]] in Its place.{{r|War Machine Vol 1 18}} the Model 11 was eventually found by [[Parnell Jacobs (Earth-616)|Parnell Jacobs]], whom with aid from [[Stuart Clarke (Earth-616)|Stuart Clarke]] sold the armor to [[Baintronics, Inc.|Baintronics]], with the armor being converted to Baintronics technology, Jacobs started using the armor in multiple clashes with Iron Man as a mercenary for [[Sunset Bain (Earth-616)|Sunset Bain]].{{r|Iron Man Vol 3 18}}

Recently, Rhodes returned using the Model 11.{{r|Invincible Iron Man Vol 5 15}}

[[File:Iron Man Armor Model 11 MK I.jpg|thumb|left|MK I]]
| Properties       =
It possesses various weapons: repulsors, unibeam (added for Rhodes), twin chain gun, laser blade, wrist-mounted flamethrower.

The shoulder pack can deploy Gatling guns, a box rocket launcher, a pulse cannon, and a plasma cannon. 

Various munitions are available: depleted uranium, high explosive, concussion, thermite, tear gas, tracer, flare, smoke, anti-tank, anti-ship, flame, fire suppressant, radio repeater or sub-nuke. Several non-lethal options were later added into the suit's MK II: baton, sabot, and rubber slugs for the cannon, concussion pulses from the hands, and strobes via the unibeam.{{r|War Machine Vol 1 16}} The armor comes equipped with a magnet in its hand and state-of-the-art wound coagulant that is administered via needle from the gauntlet.{{r|West Coast Avengers Vol 4 9}}

This model has more plating and shielding than the typical Iron Man armor. A poly-carbonate coating further improves the surface. An additional poly-prismatic coating was temporarily used to counter the [[Arthur Parks (Earth-616)|Living Laser]]'s powers. It presumably retained the photon shield from previous armors. The armor could withstand a bomb made from a higher yield of the [[Simon Williams (Earth-616)|Wonder Man]]'s energy at point-blank range.{{r|West Coast Avengers Vol 4 9}}

| History                 = This armor was a modular component system rather than a fully integrated suit. As such, each individual system (helmet, boots etc.) may have had different features.

[[File:Iron Man Armor Model 13 from All-New Manual Vol 1 1 002.jpg|thumb|left|Hulkbuster add-on.]]
There were also plug-in points for various modules. One of these was the Hulkbuster add-on used when [[Bruce Banner (Earth-616)|Hulk]] confronted [[Anthony Stark (Earth-616)|Iron Man]] over the production of gamma bombs when part of [[Stane International (Earth-616)|Stane International]]. The two met at a production plant. Stark acknowledged that [[Obadiah Stane (Earth-616)|Stane]] had conducted many illegal and unethical operations, but explained that this news was nothing more than a smear campaign. The two were able to settle the dispute and dismantle the plant.{{r|Iron Man Vol 1 305}}

| Properties       =
Repulsors and the uni-beam remained standard for the base unit. Boot jets were upgraded. A refractive coating helped against energy attacks.

Magnets located on the palms and soles as well as a grappling hook with cable were used for climbing. A loudspeaker was used to address crowds. Image inducers were upgraded to give off 'identifier signals,' fooling the [[Basil Sandhurst (Earth-616)|Controller]].

Various modules were available:
* Full Spectrum Scanalyzer with [[Adamantium]]-Tipped probe.{{r|Iron Man Vol 1 300}}
* Magnetic Railgun Launcher with explosive shells.{{r|Iron Man Vol 1 300}}
* Semi-Fluid Polymer Compound:{{r|Iron Man Vol 1 300}} energy-absorbent compound that shot out and covered its target.
* EM Field Generator:{{r|Iron Man Vol 1 300}} attracted a lightning bolt to short out [[Ultimo (Earth-616)|Ultimo]].
* Gravimetric Field Generator:{{r|Iron Man Vol 1 300}} canceled out the pull of the Earth's gravity on whatever it was attached to. 
* Polybond Adhesive Compound.{{r|Iron Man Vol 1 300}}
* Cryogenic Compact Module.{{r|Iron Man Vol 1 300}}
* Magnetic Compact Module:{{r|Iron Man Vol 1 300}} used magnetic field to polarize the target. Multiple modules could be used to polarize the target with mutually opposing states making the atoms of the target repel one another.
* Hypodermic Injector.{{r|Iron Man Vol 1 300}}
* Microsurgery Equipment.{{r|Iron Man Vol 1 314}}
* Shoulder Mounted Weapons.{{r|Iron Man Vol 1 308}}
* Hulkbuster, it integrated a ''magno-hydraulic pseudo-musculature'' which provided greatly enhanced strength rated at 175 tons. Sensors were adapted to focus on detecting gamma radiation. It had impact-resistant carbon composite plating and an anchoring system.

==Alternate Realities== 

===Year of 2020 ([[Earth-8410]])===
[[File:Anthony Stark (Earth-8410) from Iron Man 2020 Vol 1 1 0002.jpg|thumb|right]]
[[Anthony Stark (Earth-8410)|Howard]] had the armor stored.{{r|Iron Man 2020 Vol 1 1}}
{{clear}}
----
===Captain America revived today ([[Earth-11947]])===
[[File:Anthony Stark (Earth-11947) from What If...? Vol 1 68 0001.jpg|thumb|right]]
In this reality, [[Anthony Stark (Earth-11947)|Iron Man]] and the Avengers were able to capture [[Namor McKenzie (Earth-11947)|Namor]], preventing him from finding [[Steven Rogers (Earth-11947)|Captain America]] and recovering him from the ice. This meant Captain America was unable to stop the [[Sleepers (Robots)|Nazi Sleeper robots]]. After the [[Johann Shmidt (Earth-11947)|Red Skull]] and the [[National Socialist German Workers Party (Earth-11947)|Nazi's]] conquered America, Iron Man joined the [[X-Patriots (Earth-11947)|X-Patriots]] and helped in the final assault against the Red Skull's force. He helped free the [[Bruce Banner (Earth-11947)|Hulk]] from the Nazi's mental enslavement before his armor ran out of power.{{r|What If...? Vol 1 67|68}}
{{clear}}
----

===Marvel Vs. Capcom ([[Earth-30847]])===
[[File:Anthony Stark (Earth-30847) from Marvel vs. Capcom 2 New Age of Heroes 0001.jpg|thumb|right]]
In this reality, [[Anthony Stark (Earth-11947)|Iron Man]] had the model 13 as one of his many armors.
{{clear}}
----

===Spider-Man's Parents Destroyed His Family ([[Earth-94561]])===
[[File:Anthony Stark (Earth-94561) from What If...? Vol 1 61 0001.jpg|thumb|right]]
In this reality, [[Anthony Stark (Earth-94561)|Iron Man]] shared a similar history to his [[Anthony Stark (Earth-616)|Prime Universe]] counterpart until [[Peter Parker (Earth-94561)|Spider-Man]] was persued for the deaths of [[Mary Jane Watson (Earth-94561)|Mary Jane Watson]] and [[Maybelle Parker (Earth-94561)|Aunt May]]. He was one of the many heroes who discovered Spider-Man and the bodies of his "parents" [[Richard Parker (Simulacrum) (Earth-94561)|"Richard"]] and [[Mary Parker (Simulacrum) (Earth-94561)|"Mary"]].{{r|What If...? Vol 1 61}}
{{clear}}
----

===The Marvel Action Hour ([[Earth-94561]])===
[[File:Anthony Stark (Earth-534834) from Iron Man The Animated Series Season 2 12 001.png|thumb|right]]
In this reality, [[Anthony Stark (Earth-534834)|Iron Man]] utilized the Modular Armor as his main suit.
{{clear}}

| CurrentOwner            = [[Anthony Stark (Earth-616)|Tony Stark]]
| PreviousOwners          = 

| Notes                   = * The official stance whether this armor's Hulkbuster add-on is considered a subset of the Model 13 or its own individual suit has fluctuated over the years. It was originally identified as the distinct Model 14 in 2008's [[All-New Iron Manual Vol 1 1|''All-New Iron Manual'']]. It was reidentified as a subset of the Model 13 in the [[Iron Manual TPB Vol 1 1|''Iron Manual'' TPB]], released later that year. In 2018's [[:Category:Many Armors of Iron Man Variants|"Many Armors of Iron Man"]] variant cover series for {{cl|Tony Stark: Iron Man Vol 1 1}}, it was split back into Models 13 and 14. The cover series implies other changes, as the designations for Models [[Iron Man Armor Model 42|42]], [[Iron Man Armor Model 45|45]], [[Iron Man Armor Model 50|50]] and [[Iron Man Armor Model 51|51]] remain unchanged despite the Model 13 split bumping up the designations for Models [[Iron Man Armor Model 16|16]], [[Iron Man Armor Model 22|22]], [[Iron Man Armor Model 29|29]] and [[Iron Man Armor Model 37|37]] (to 17, 23, 30 and 38, respectively). Since the limited scope of the cover series makes it impossible to determine the full extent of changes in numeration (as it only spotlighted twenty suits), the Marvel Database will prioritize the numbering from the ''Iron Manual'' TPB.
| Trivia                  = * The Modular Armor is quite popular as it was/is usually used by the [[Iron Man: The Animated Series|1990s animated version]] of [[Anthony Stark (Earth-534834)|Iron Man]] and [[Earth-30847|Capcom video games 90s-2000s version]] of [[Anthony Stark (Earth-30847)|Iron Man]].

The armor had oversize gauntlets with wrist-top projectors. They could also be remotely controlled by Iron Man when not attached to the suit. ''Wide angle'' repulsors fired over more surface area. | History                 = When Stark realized he had sold [[Justin Hammer]] all copies of the [[Evader Armor]], he went to confront Hammer on his orbiting space station using this suit.

==Capabilities==
This armor emphasizes stealth, and seems to be designed to function in space only. It is less durable than earlier designs but is stealthier and easier to control.  

The armor is covered with an experimental compression gel before launching. It uses a [[Stark Booster Rocket|booster rig]] with solid-fuel rockets rather than its own supply to leave Earth's atmosphere.
 
Instead of traditional boot jets, the suit uses compressed gas maneuvering pods. Retro burst stabilizers located at the knees and hips help maintain attitude control.

A solar sail assists in both reentry and recharging the armor.

It possesses {{Power|Repulsor Ray|repulsors}}, a uni-beam, pulse bolts and explosive 'concussion buds.'

ECM jamming and a stealth mode mask its presence. It possesses various sensors including a thermal scan.

Like other space armors, auto-sealants protect the wearer and an autopilot can return it to Earth.

[[File:Anthony Stark (Earth-616) from Iron Man Vol 3 44 002.jpg|thumb|left]]
In light of Ultron's attempting to use S.K.I.N. as a weapon of mass destruction, Tony had abandoned use of this armor and constructed the [[Iron Man Armor Model 20]].

==Capabilities==
S.K.I.N. is a flexible alloy that can bounce like a basketball yet become nearly as hard as [[Adamantium]]. On command S.K.I.N. flows out of the chest plate and forms the gold armor sections. [[Jocasta Pym (Earth-616)|Jocasta]]'s AI served as the armor's operating system. Sensors and circuitry were improved as a whole. The new "Stark Card" was integrated into the system. Repulsors and pulse bolts are standard weaponry. A new energy absorber is able to take in energy and fire it back out via the "omnibeam." The sonic array and tractor beam are improved.

[[File:Anthony Stark (Earth-616) from Iron Man Vol 3 44 001.jpg|thumb|right]]
The energy blade in the gauntlet doubles as a weapon and an [[Energy Shield]]. The small shields can extend to cover the entire armor, but are less potent. Probes launched from the gauntlets provide many functions: they have limited repulsors of their own, image inducers, a sensor array, and can detonate as "smart bombs." A newer version of the "chameleon effect" provides cloaking at the cost of expending considerable power. If need be, the armor can enter an emergency mode where it will automatically find a safe place, cloak, and power down.

| History                 = The armor's energy intake was very efficient compared to past models; even small appliances could produce a decent recharge for the armor. It was significantly overhauled after Iron Man's first battle with [[Temugin (Earth-616)|Temugin]]. The armor was overtaken by an alien nanoplasm, causing Tony to remotely trigger the self-destruct system. Subsequent armors, such as the [[Iron Secretary Armor|armor]] worn while Stark was Secretary of Defense, remained similar to this design.

[[File:Iron Man Vol 3 52 Textless.jpg|thumb|left]]
==Capabilities==
Repulsors were modified including a mild version for 'crowd control' as well as improvements when fired underwater and in space. Firing repulsors and uni-beam simultaneously produced a "blockbusting" effect.{{r|Iron Man Vol 3 50}} Sonic weapons were improved.  A deflector pulse can push objects away from the armor. A magnetic pulse was developed for specific use against the [[Mandarin's Rings|Makluan Power Rings]]. Defensively, EMP shielding was improved. The basic forcefield used wave algorithms to randomly change its frequency. A small energy shield could be emitted from the gauntlets.  Backup forcefields could also be used to cover armor breaches. [[Anthony Masters (Earth-616)|Taskmaster]] admitted he couldn't defeat Iron Man hand-to-hand.{{r|Taskmaster Vol 1 1}}

For security purposes the armor was encoded to Stark's artificial heart. An emergency override key was given to [[Virginia Potts (Earth-616)|Pepper Potts]]. Liquid oxygen cells provided an improved air supply underwater and in space, but were dangerous if ruptured. Under normal conditions a respirator took in and purified outside air. A carbon dioxide mix was used for improved underwater propulsion. A searchlight for the helmet was also available for underwater missions.{{r|Iron Man Vol 3 63}} Utility tools in the left gauntlet could be used for repairs, bomb disposal, or other tasks. A number of software upgrades were included in the armor, particularly in the sensor array and diagnostics. Notably, the incorporation of GPS technology and an ionic mist spray used to mark objects.

| History                 = [[Thor Odinson (Earth-616)|Thor]], God of Thunder, provided [[Anthony Stark (Earth-616)|Tony Stark]] with an [[Asgard|Asgardian]] crystal charged with immense energy to study. The hope was that its power could act as a safer, cleaner energy source than the current technology on Earth possessed.

Asgard moved over [[Slokovia]] after Asgardian worshipers were killed. Storms raged and the Valkyrior were sent to collect the dead. [[Victor von Doom (Earth-616)|Doctor Doom]] was secretly manipulating events, supplying one group with weapons while offering the others asylum in [[Latveria]]. 

[[File:Thor God of Thunder Vol 1 7 Many Armors of Iron Man Variant Textless.jpg|thumb|left]]
Stark was asked by the US government to talk to Thor and convince him to leave before United Nations forces entered the area. Thor refused to do so. 

Doom then contacted Stark and told him he would need to use the crystal to have any chance at stopping Thor, who now wielded his father's [[Odin-Force]] in addition to his already great power.

Stark designed the Thorbuster armor, giving it a look somewhat similar to the [[Destroyer (Enchanted Armor)|Destroyer armor]] and used it in a confrontation with Thor. Thor was surprised at its power and that Tony would turn a 'gift from the gods into a weapon.' He destroyed the reactor and Iron Man ejected from it. 

Only the intervention of [[Steven Rogers (Earth-616)|Captain America]] was sufficient to prevent military involvement. He too tried to talk Thor down, but got his [[Captain America's Shield|shield]] dented in the process. When Thor realized he was attacking his old friends, he stopped. After repairing Cap's shield, he moved Asgard away from the area.  

Doom was able to gain the design plans for the reactor, but Stark countered by infecting his systems with a computer virus.

| Properties              = 
The armor was powered by an Asgardian mystical element. Everything from flight to life support utilized the magical energy. A facemask could be lowered for additional protection. If need be the wearer could eject and use a normal Iron Man armor.

Experimental "Type X" repulsors could be used to boost the armor's punches in addition to the standard blast. The uni-beam fired large bursts of energy. Also impervious to any kinds of harm except, oddly enough, Thor.

The Asgardian Crystal empowers the armor and allows it to absorb and manipulate Asgardian energies effectively giving him Odin Force. It was even able to stop [[Mjolnir]] in mid-flight. 

| Notes                   = * This armor was originally identified as the Iron Man Armor Model 23 in 2008's [[All-New Iron Manual Vol 1 1|''All-New Iron Manual'']]. It was subsequently renumbered to Model 22 in the [[Iron Manual TPB Vol 1 1|''Iron Manual'' TPB]], released later that year, due to the reclassification of the previously-designated Model 14 as a subset of the [[Iron Man Armor Model 13|Model 13]]. It was also durable enough to take several blows from [[Ultimo (Earth-616)|Ultimo]], although the armor was severely damaged afterward. | Origin                  = [[Anthony Stark (Earth-616)|Tony Stark]] was approached by the US government on developing a suit to protect vital employees from a nuclear attack. [[Bruce Banner (Earth-616)|Bruce Banner]] was also asked to provide his input on protecting the suit from gamma radiation.

Banner's addition was "RG-27", a special compound that neutralizes gamma radiation. Since it is most effective in liquid or gas form, a series of tubes were built into the armor for irrigation. This enables the armor not only to withstand radiation, but also allows it to decontaminate areas.

To expose a government conspiracy, the two faked a quarrel over some of their designs. Stark unveiled a finished version of the suit to battle the Hulk. 

However, Stark seemed to be acting strangely while wearing the suit. A problem with the irrigation system was discovered. The Hulk was able to help Stark shut it down before gamma poisoning set in.

==Capabilities==
The armor is designed to attract radiation into the armor where it is converted into usable power. This greatly enhances its strength.

Through absorbing ambient radiation the armor is able to decontaminate irradiated areas.
 
It also possesses repulsors and a unibeam.

[[Andrew Stockwell (Earth-616)|Titanium Man]] stowed away on the ship and attempted to sabotage the operation but failed.

==Capabilities==
This armor was designed for the increased gravity conditions of hyperspace travel. Its limits were unknown, but Tony was safe at 50 Gs. The design made sure that blood remained in the limbs rather than collecting in the torso.

A combination of pseudo-musculature, mobility software and a magnetic/jet compensator helped the wearer move around.

Tony was still affected by G-Loc (loss of consciousness), possible nitrogen narcosis, and ''the bends'', all of which were side-effects of hyper-gravity travel. If he became sick, the armor cleaned and disinfected itself.

An intermix mask worn under the helmet regulated oxygen, as normal air under high gravity condition was dangerous.

It was unknown if this armor could fly. 

Weapons systems were unknown; presumably it had functioning repulsors and a uni-beam.

pages.wikitext:

| Origin                  = Stark's latest test model tested new technologies designed on speed. Not just in terms of travel, but in the response time between the wearer's thought and the armor's action.
| Type                    = Iron Man Armor
| Dimensions              = 
| Weight                  = 200 lbs.{{r|Iron Man: Hypervelocity Vol 1 6}}
| Creators                = Adam Warren
| First                   = Iron Man: Hypervelocity Vol 1 1

| History                 = This armor was created by [[Anthony Stark (Earth-616)|Tony Stark]], based partially in reverse-engineered and extrapolated supervillain hardware. Compared to previous models, this armor features a radical increase in computing power, to enable tactical autonomy if its user was incapacitated or killed while wearing it. When Stark came under attack by the mech tribe known as the [[Beautiful Garbage (Earth-616)|Beautiful Garbage]], a digital copy of Stark's mind named "[[Tony Stark 2.0 (Earth-616)|Tony Stark 2.0]]" went into action on its own, and set out to find the responsibles for the attack. However, to S.H.I.E.L.D. was sent a modified video message in which Tony 2.0 was framed for Stark's severe injury, for which Iron Man 2.0 was forced to confront the [[Superhuman Restraint Unit (Earth-616)|Capekiller unit]].{{r|Iron Man: Hypervelocity Vol 1 2}} When the Beautiful Garbage attacked the Capekiller's [[Assault Carrier Samuel Sawyer|Assault Carrier]], a thermonuclear warhead was activated as a contingecy plan. With only 0.009 seconds to manually deactivate the device, Iron Man 2.0 might or might not have been destroyed along with the armor.{{r|Iron Man: Hypervelocity Vol 1 6}}

==Capabilities==
The armor's main feature is the presence of high-speed hardware,{{r|Iron Man: Hypervelocity Vol 1 1}} being able to move at speeds more than 150% faster than a regular Iron Man suit when using its "accelerationware."{{r|Iron Man: Hypervelocity Vol 1 6}} Additonally, the armor was capable of analyzing and learning from its wearer as well as following routines such as autopilot. In emergency situations, it can "upload" a copy of the consciousness of its wearer into its systems. Boot jets were variable mode and automatically adapted to environmental changes such as lack of air. For high speed underwater, the armor used a supercativation spike.{{r|Iron Man: Hypervelocity Vol 1 2}}

A capacitor ring mounted in the back stored and regulated the suit's power, it could launch tungsten-carbide rounds at hypersonic speeds.{{r|Iron Man: Hypervelocity Vol 1 5}} Manipulators mounted in the arms fired {{Power|Repulsor Ray|repulsors}}. Plates on the knuckles could generate a powerful electric shock. "Impact studs" can extend from the elbows. The armor's uni-beam seemed to be standard issue.{{r|Iron Man: Hypervelocity Vol 1 2}} Penetrator fletchettes could also be fired in bursts from the gauntlets. The armor could also fire narrow-focus electromagnetic pulse discharges.{{r|Iron Man: Hypervelocity Vol 1 6}} The armor's outer shell could be used to generate resonance. While Stark used it initially for broadcasting music, it could be turned into a potent sonic weapon.{{r|Iron Man: Hypervelocity Vol 1 3}} For defensive purposes, the armor had "chameleonware" cloaking as well as chaff and flares.{{r|Iron Man: Hypervelocity Vol 1 4}}

| PreviousOwners          = [[Anthony Stark (Earth-616)|Tony Stark]]

It was subsequently renumbered to Model 28 in the [[Iron Manual TPB Vol 1 1|''Iron Manual'' TPB]], released later that year, due to the reclassification of the previously-designated Model 14 as a subset of the [[Iron Man Armor Model 13|Model 13]]. {{sld|Iron Man: Enter the Mandarin Vol 1 4}}{{g|Chronologically}} | Destruction = | History = [[File:Anthony Stark (Earth-616) from Iron Man Vol 1 55 001.jpg|thumb|left|Tony assembles the armor]] This armor was built by [[Anthony Stark (Earth-616)|Tony Stark]] after his previous defeat at the hands of the [[Mandarin (Earth-616)|Mandarin]].{{r|Iron Man: Enter the Mandarin Vol 1 4}} The new generation of Iron Man armors started with this model, by implementing a long time staple of the Iron Man arsenal: Repulsor Rays.{{r|Tales of Suspense Vol 1 67}} Shortly after, Tony decided to give his armor more facial features, by including the infamous faceplate which included a "nose".{{r|Iron Man Vol 1 68}} When [[Harold Hogan (Earth-616)|Happy Hogan]] was captured by the [[Mandarin]] while wearing this armor, Tony created the Model 3 MK II (unofficial designation) which was "strong enough to overcome the handicap of [his] newly-injured heart".{{r|Tales of Suspense Vol 1 85}} Later, it was heavily damaged in a battle against [[Harold Hogan (Earth-616)|The Freak]], forcing Tony to create the [[Iron Man Armor Model 4|Model 4 armor]], which was not only more flexible, but also returned to the nose-less faceplate.{{r|Iron Man Vol 1 85}} It was briefly used by [[Happy Hogan]] and [[Guardsman (Michael O'Brien)|Michael O'Brien]] as well. When [[Anthony Stark (Earth-616)|Tony Stark]] undertook Stark Resilient, he dismantled and melted one of the models of this armor.{{r|Invincible Iron Man Vol 2 26}} | Properties = The armor was durable enough to stay in close proximity to a burning asteroid and survive a fall from the stratosphere into the ocean floor.{{r|I Am Iron Man Vol 1 2}} The armor was upgraded with more backup power to let [[Anthony Stark (Earth-616)|Tony Stark]] live for several minutes underwater.{{r|I Am Iron Man Vol 1 2}} The Armor possesses atributes basic to all Iron Man Armors: * '''{{Power|Superhuman Strength}}''' * '''{{Power|Superhuman Durability}}''' * '''{{Power|Superhuman Speed}}''' * '''{{Power|Energy Projection}}''' * '''{{Power|Self-Propelled Flight}}''' The armor comes equipped with the following: *Image inducer produced holograms. *Electric bolts could be used for stunning. *The armor's surface could be heated. *Various gadgets: vapor ejector, smoke bombs, bomb pellets, a chemical kit, cutting blade, sound duplicator, and a high frequency wave generator. *Life support was improved with a longer air supply. *The armor could absorb energy from extreme temperatures (both hot and cold) and could be used to amplify certain features of the armor, an example being thruster power.{{r|I Am Iron Man Vol 1 2}} *The armor included the infamous rocket skates as a back-up way of transportation.{{r|Iron Man Vol 1 85}} * '''{{Power|Regeneration|Self Repair}}'''{{r|Iron Man Vol 1 49}} | Notes = * The 2008 [[Iron Manual TPB Vol 1 1|"Iron Manual"]] states that Iron Man's Model 4 armor first appeared in {{cl|Tales of Suspense Vol 1 85}}, but this issue actually shows the creation of Model 3 MK II (unofficial designation). The Model 3 armor continued to be used until {{cl|Iron Man Vol 1 85}}. * The Iron Man armor, especially the models prior to the Model 3, were in a constant state of experimentation and improvement. The Model 3 distinguished itself when Anthony Stark implements a basic helmet design. The Model 2 helmet first had a horned look. The helmet mask was later riveted on flat. The Model 3 appears to be of a smooth bore motif which led to Iron Man being affectionately referred to by some of his fellow Avengers as "Shell-Head". The Model 4 removed the 'nose' and initially could be worn in a soft state under clothing which hardened and expanded when needed. | Trivia = * Tony says he "may have been drinking when [he] thought of" the idea of rocket skates.{{r|A + X Vol 1 17}} | Links = }} [[it:Armatura Iron Man Modello 3]]
