pages.title: Iron Man Armor Model 72
pages.wikitext:
{{Marvel Database: Item Template | Title = [[Iron Man Armor|Iron Man Armor Model 72
(Mysterium Armor)]] | Image = Iron Man Armor Model 72 from Avengers Vol 9 31 Vecchio Variant cover.jpg | Name = [[Iron Man Armor|Iron Man Armor Model 72]] | Aliases = Mysterium Armor{{r|Iron Man Vol 6 1}} | CurrentOwner = [[Anthony Stark (Earth-616)|Tony Stark]] | PreviousOwners = | AlternateOwners = | Type = Iron Man Armor | Material = [[Mysterium (Metal)|Mysterium]] | Dimensions = | Weight = | Origin = | Reality = Earth-616 | LeadDesigner = [[Anthony Stark (Earth-616)|Tony Stark]] | AdditionalDesigners = | PlaceOfCreation = [[Hellfire Club Building|Hellfire Club]], [[Manhattan]], [[New York City]], [[New York (State)|New York]] | PlaceOfDestruction = | Creators = Gerry Duggan; Pepe Larraz | First = Invincible Iron Man Vol 5 15 | History = Following the hostile takeover of [[Stark Unlimited (Earth-616)|Stark Unlimited]] by the human supremacist tycoon [[Kelvin Heng (Earth-616)|Feilong]], [[Anthony Stark (Earth-616)|Tony Stark]] saw his technological resources being put to the service of a quest of anti-mutant oppression orchestrated by the think tank [[Orchis (Earth-616)|Orchis]], namely by Feilong's design and mass-production of a new type of [[Sentinels|Sentinel]] outfitted with Iron Man technology that he dubbed the [[Stark Sentinel MK II|Stark Sentinels]].{{r|Invincible Iron Man Vol 5 7}} The strength of Orchis' campaign of terror forced the [[X-Men (Earth-616)|X-Men]] into hiding. Stark joined them in secrecy since he couldn't legally continue operating as Iron Man due to Feilong owning his patents, and began operating out of the [[Hellfire Club Building|Hellfire Club]].{{r|Invincible Iron Man Vol 5 9}} After discovering that a theoretical metal discovered in the past by his father [[Howard Stark (Earth-616)|Howard]] was nothing other than the mutant-harvested [[Mysterium (Metal)|mysterium]], Tony sought to use it to craft his countermeasure against Feilong's Stark Sentinels.{{r|Invincible Iron Man Vol 5 10}} The end result of Stark's designs was a skyscraper-sized [[Iron Man Armor Model 73|Sentinel Buster Armor]], with the human-sized Model 72 serving as a flight suit for it.{{r|Invincible Iron Man Vol 5 15}} Iron Man and [[Emma Frost (Earth-616)|Emma Frost]] retrieved the mysterium deposited by the X-Men in [[Gameworld]], sending most of it to [[Nidavellir]] to be forged into the Sentinel Buster by [[Riri Williams (Earth-616)|Ironheart]], and keeping enough to use a fabricator stolen from [[Stane International (Earth-616)|Stane International]] to craft the Model 72.{{r|Invincible Iron Man Vol 5 13}} Stark first debuted the Mysterium Armor during the day of reckoning against Orchis, suiting up ahead of time to defend himself and Frost from a [[Sentinel Zero]] sent to the Hellfire Club to kill Tony. Iron Man subsequently convened with the Sentinel Buster in the [[Australia]]n Outback, which landed split into parts and disguised as ships meant to trick Orchis into thinking they were transporting the mutant counter-offensive, in order to lure the Stark Sentinels armada to a trap.{{r|Invincible Iron Man Vol 5 15}} Tony briefly kept the Mysterium Armor as his standard suit.{{r|Avengers Vol 9 17|to=23}} However, due to word spreading about it, Stark shelved it into a warehouse in [[Long Island City]]. As part of an alliance between [[Advanced Idea Mechanics (Earth-616)|A.I.M.]] and [[Roxxon Energy Corporation (Earth-616)|Roxxon]], [[Justine Hammer (Earth-616)|Justine Hammer]] exploited the armor's disuse and stole it. She cannibalized it for its mysterium to finish an [[Iron Monger Armor MK III|Iron Monger Armor]] for herself.{{r|Iron Man Vol 6 1}} Some time later, Tony somehow regained the Mysterium Armor,{{r|Avengers Vol 9 29}} but retired the suit in favor of the new [[Iron Man Armor Model 75|Model 75 Armor]].{{r|Iron Man Vol 7 1}} | Properties = ===Overview=== Although the Model 72 was conceived with the primary function to serve as the pilot suit for the behemothic [[Iron Man Armor Model 73|Sentinel Buster]], it was nevertheless poised to be one of [[Anthony Stark (Earth-616)|Iron Man]]'s strongest normal-sized suits, since it was built using [[Mysterium (Metal)|mysterium]], a hyper-conductive "miracle metal." It possessed the standard abilities of a regular Iron Man Armor, including flight, enhanced strength and repulsor blasts. Its suit-up was achieved automatically via self-propelled flight of the armor's constituent parts,{{r|Invincible Iron Man Vol 5 15}} which could also be commanded to encase different targets.{{r|West Coast Avengers Vol 4 4}} In terms of secondary systems and gadgets, the Mysterium Armor possessed comms systems{{r|Invincible Iron Man Vol 5 19}} which could tap into all broadcast systems worldwide,{{r|Blood Hunt Vol 1 3}} a pair of pop-out air coolants,{{r|Invincible Iron Man Vol 5 18}} holographic projectors,{{r|Invincible Iron Man Vol 5 19}} an index finger-mounted flamethrower, the ability to shoot a flash-drying amber-like gunk to immobilize targets,{{r|Invincible Iron Man Vol 5 20}} the ability to generate and control magnetic fields,{{r|Blood Hunt Vol 1 2}} first aid,{{r|Blood Hunt Vol 1 5}} secondary thrusters on the shins and back,{{r|Avengers Vol 9 12}}{{r|Avengers Vol 9 13}} and life support that allows the user to operate comfortably in space.{{r|Avengers Vol 9 13}} [[File:Anthony Stark (Earth-616) from Invincible Iron Man Vol 5 15 002.jpg|thumb|250px|right|Withstanding adamantium claws]] ===Offensive Powers=== The armor derived much of its physical power from mysterium, allowing it to cleanly knock the head off a [[Stark Sentinel MK II|Stark Sentinel]] with a single punch, whereas previous iterations of the Iron Man Armor struggled to fight a single one of these robots.{{r|Invincible Iron Man Vol 5 19}} Due to the mysterium's hyper-conductivity, the Model 72 could discharge more pure energy than any Iron Man suit ever had before.{{r|Invincible Iron Man Vol 5 18}} In addition to repulsor blasts, the Mysterium Armor possessed missiles mounted on its shoulders and the side of its torso. A single deployment of this ordnance combined with repulsor rays was capable of critically damaging a Stark Sentinel.{{r|Invincible Iron Man Vol 5 19}} The armor's wrists also concealed a pair of pop-out blasters.{{r|Avengers Vol 9 12}} The armor's back concealed a pop-out blaster.{{r|Avengers Vol 9 30}} The armor's wrist concealed pop-out ray guns.{{r|Avengers Vol 9 32}} ===Defensive Powers=== The Model 72 was virtually imprevious to most types of damage due to the natural properties of mysterium, making it more durable than [[adamantium]], which crushed on impact with it, and unaffected by magic.{{r|Invincible Iron Man Vol 5 15}} The armor could survive reentry from space with ease{{r|Invincible Iron Man Vol 5 19}} and effectively take a hit from blasts from powerful machines like the [[War Machine Sentinel]], a specially modified Stark Sentinel.{{r|Invincible Iron Man Vol 5 16}} The armor was also specifically designed with energy shielding imprevious from [[Kelvin Heng (Earth-616)|Feilong]]'s concussive beam.{{r|Invincible Iron Man Vol 5 16}} The armor, however, could be compromised by exploiting its intrinsic properties, such as when the vampire [[Cruel (Vampire) (Earth-616)|Cruel]] used telekinetically controlled razor wire to burrow into the armor through the joints of its plating.{{r|Blood Hunt Vol 1 1}} The armor can form layered electromagnetic shielding.{{r|Avengers Vol 9 30}} {{Clear}} | AlternateVersions = | Notes = | Trivia = * Artist [[Pepe Larraz]] was chosen to design the Mysterium Armor because he needed to start drawing May 2024's {{cl|Blood Hunt Vol 1}}, which features [[Anthony Stark (Earth-616)|Iron Man]] alongside the [[Avengers (Earth-616)|Avengers]], ahead of its debut in {{cl|Invincible Iron Man Vol 5}}. ''Invincible Iron Man'' writer [[Gerry Duggan]] and his collaborators had yet to design the hero's new look for the third arc of Duggan's run. A contributing factor was Larraz and Duggan's previous collaboration in {{cl|Planet-Size X-Men Vol 1 1}} and {{cl|X-Men Vol 6}}.{{cite|ref=true|url=https://gerryduggan.substack.com/p/meet-the-mark-72-mysterium-armor|title=Meet The Mark 72: Mysterium Armor|work=Substack|first=Gerry|last=Duggan|date=December 22, 2023|accessdate=March 29, 2024|archiveurl=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/8r4jO|archivedate=March 29, 2024}} * Larraz has provided the following insights into the design of the Mysterium Armor: ** He designed it with the main idea that an Iron Man Armor must have more to do with a high-end sports car than a tactical body suit. His first drafts were headed in that direction until his friend and fellow artist [[David López]] argued that they made Iron Man look like a [[w:c:transformers:Transformers (franchise)|Transformer]]. ** Despite his limited experience drawing Iron Man, Larraz concluded that the most iconic part in every iteration was the chest and legs, so he focused on finding an iconic shape for the chest and the unibeam, as well as a recognizable silhouette. ** He encountered a problem designing the waist, arguing that the appropriate shape to facilitate movement could "easily look like a petrified solid diapers, or a very bold swimsuit." He solved this issue by leaving that part in a complete black area, which also helped create a black shape that made it easy for artists to draw him and readers to follow him around the page. Larraz also stated that it made sense as a reference to "the darkness of the mysterium." ** Among variations that circled around the final design, Larraz tried giving the suit a black faceplate, which he felt looked like [[War Machine]], and making it more bulky. He didn't like the last one, believing that an Iron Man suit should look "robust but agile." ** Editor [[Tom Brevoort]] asked Larraz to articulate the waist area with plates in order not to lose the feeling of armor. He and Larraz also decided to give the suit a chrome finish, which was "more minimal and it looks more expensive and sophisticated. All very Tony Stark." ** The final pass at the armor's design included gold lines from his initial inspiration of cars in order to "remark the high end, exclusive custom trait of the object. It's an Iron Man armor, it's priceless."{{cite|ref=true|url=https://twitter.com/PepeLarraz/status/1738638563774746710|title=PepeLarraz on X: "Some months ago @Marvel asked me to design the newest iteration of the ...|work=X|first=Pepe|last=Larraz|date=December 23, 2023|accessdate=March 29, 2024|archiveurl=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/JSfGB|archivedate=March 29, 2024}} * This armor appears to have been erroneously used throughout the {{cl|Ultraman X Avengers Vol 1}} crossover, having changed from Model 70 before changing color schemes back to Model 70's colors. Another clue evident of this is that all of the covers for each of the four issues feature Model 70 instead of Model 72. | Links = }} [[Category:Mysterium]]

(Sentinel Buster Armor)]] | Image = Iron Man Armor Model 73 from Invincible Iron Man Vol 5 15 001.jpg | Name = [[Iron Man Armor|Iron Man Armor Model 73]] | Aliases = | CurrentOwner = [[Anthony Stark (Earth-616)|Tony Stark]] | PreviousOwners = | AlternateOwners = | Type = Iron Man Armor | Material = [[Mysterium]] | Dimensions = | Weight = | Origin = | Reality = Earth-616 | LeadDesigner = [[Anthony Stark (Earth-616)|Tony Stark]] | AdditionalDesigners = | PlaceOfCreation = [[Furnaces of Nidavellir]], [[Nidavellir]] | PlaceOfDestruction = | Creators = Gerry Duggan; Juan Frigeri | First = Invincible Iron Man Vol 5 14 | First2 = (In disguise)
{{sld|Invincible Iron Man Vol 5 15}}(Full appearance) | History = After the human supremacist mogul [[Kelvin Heng (Earth-616)|Feilong]] seized control of [[Stark Unlimited (Earth-616)|Stark Unlimited]] and poured its resources into the creation of [[Stark Sentinel MK II|Stark Sentinels]] to fuel [[Orchis (Earth-616)|Orchis]]' campaign of mutant prosecution, [[Anthony Stark (Earth-616)|Tony Stark]] joined forces with the runaway [[X-Men (Earth-616)|X-Men]] in secrecy, since he couldn't legally operate as Iron Man due to Feilong owning the patents of his technology.{{r|Invincible Iron Man Vol 5 9}} During his alliance with the mutant telepath [[Emma Frost (Earth-616)|Emma Frost]], Stark learned that a theoretical metal discovered by his father [[Howard Stark (Earth-616)|Howard]] in the past was none other than the mutant-harvested [[Mysterium]], so Tony sought to use it to craft his countermeasures against Feilong's Stark Sentinels.{{r|Invincible Iron Man Vol 5 10}} Stark's planning efforts culminated in the design of a towering Sentinel Buster Armor meant to fight the Stark Sentinels head-on.{{r|Invincible Iron Man Vol 5 15}} In order to build it, he and Emma Frost recovered the mysterium deposited by the X-Men on [[Gameworld]] and had [[Eros (Earth-616)|Starfox]] deliver it to [[Nidavellir]]. Sharing the design of the Sentinel Buster with [[Riri Williams (Earth-616)|Ironheart]], Tony had her convene with the [[Dwarves of Nidavellir]] and construct the Sentinel Buster, by happenstance joining forces with the X-Man [[Forge (Earth-616)|Forge]]. In order to lure Orchis into a trap, the Sentinel Buster was split into separate pieces meant to resemble spaceships. The resistance fed Orchis false intel that these "ships" were going to carry a mutant armada from [[Mars (Planet)|Mars]] to [[Earth]].{{r|Invincible Iron Man Vol 5 14}} On the day of reckoning, Iron Man convened with the pieces of the Sentinel Buster in the [[Australia]]n Outback, prompting Feilong to send the majority of the Stark Sentinels to Stark's position. As they arrived, Iron Man assembled the "ships" into the Sentinel Buster.{{r|Invincible Iron Man Vol 5 15}} Stark laid waste to the Stark Sentinels, but the armor's energy demands were too much for the actual number of Stark Sentinels online. When Feilong arrived in a [[War Machine Sentinel]], the Sentinel Buster engaged him, and the villain rammed his mecha into the Sentinel Buster's chest, damaging its giant-sized [[Arc Reactor|R.T. node]] and shutting it down.{{r|Invincible Iron Man Vol 5 16}} | Properties = ===Overview=== The Sentinel Buster Armor is designed specifically to overpower [[Stark Sentinel MK II|Stark Sentinels]], dwarfing the size of these robots by an order of several magnitudes. It's made of an alloy comprised of [[Mysterium]], a hyper-conductive "miracle metal" that is more durable than [[adamantium]] and impervious to magic.{{r|Invincible Iron Man Vol 5 15}} The Sentinel Buster possesses the standard abilities of a regular Iron Man Armor, including flight, enhanced strength, repulsor blasts, and a unibeam, but scaled up. It can crush and punch through Stark Sentinels with ease, and its unibeam can disintegrate them almost instantly. The suit additionally possesses powerful missiles and flamethrowers. The massive armor is operated using the normal-sized [[Iron Man Armor Model 72|Model 72 Armor]] as a flight suit, and its systems are connected to its user through it, with the cockpit being located in the Sentinel Buster's head. However, the Sentinel Buster does possess an autopilot function. The main weakness of the Model 73 is that it is extremely power-intensive, meaning that it can only be used for a limited time before its energy is depleted.{{r|Invincible Iron Man Vol 5 16}} | AlternateVersions = | Notes = * The Sentinel Buster Armor was designed by the former regular artist of {{cl|Invincible Iron Man Vol 5}}, [[Juan Frigeri]], before leaving the book to pencil {{cl|Ultimates Vol 3}}.{{cite web|url=https://twitter.com/juanmfrigeri/status/1766478931304083615|title=Juan M Frigeri on X: "This is my design for #sentinelbuster for ...|work=X|first=Juan|last=Frigeri|date=March 9, 2024|accessdate=March 29, 2024|archiveurl=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/UafqI|archivedate=March 29, 2024}} | Trivia = * Based on [[Juan Frigeri]]'s design sheet for it, the Sentinel Buster Armor is roughly as tall as thirty-two regular-sized Iron Man suits. With the average Iron Man suit being 6'6" (1.98 m) tall,{{r|Avengers: Roll Call Vol 1 1}} this means that the height of the Sentinel Buster can be estimated to be 208' (63.4 m). | Links = }} {{DEFAULTSORT:Iron_Man_Armor_Model_073.0|noerror}} [[Category:Mysterium]]

| History                 = While Iron Man's conventional suits could function underwater, they had several limitations. Stark specially designed this armor to work underwater at depths of up to 3 miles. In terms of appearance, it was an all new design with the exception of the helmet taken from the [[Iron Man Armor Model 4|Model 4]] armor.

[[File:Captain Marvel Vol 7 12 Many Armors of Iron Man Variant Textless.jpg|thumb|left]]
==Capabilities==
All repulsor weapons are adapted for underwater use; in particular the updated "tri-beam" style uni-beam and mini torpedoes. The armor can generate an electrical field around itself similar to an electric eel. It could also release a chemical into the water that generates an inky-black cloud similar to an octopus's. Boot jets received modified turbines. Life support was enhanced for deep sea conditions. Long-range exo-units act as grapples with fully articulated hands. Crampons help in maintaining footing on rocks and coral. The backpack is a holding bay that can store objects. Lastly, the main armor can be jettisoned if needed to escape.

| CurrentOwner            = Iron Man
| PreviousOwners          = 

| Notes                   = * This armor, the [[Iron Man Armor Model 6|Stealth Armor]] and the [[Iron Man Armor Model 7|Silver Centurion Armor]] were originally identified in 1993's {{cl|Iron Manual Vol 1 1}} as Models 6, 7 and 8, respectively. However, these designations did not correspond with the chronological order in which these suits debuted ({{cl|Iron Man Vol 1 152}}, {{cl|Iron Man Vol 1 200|#200}} and {{cl|Iron Man Vol 1 218|#218}}). In 2018, the [[:Category:Many Armors of Iron Man Variants|"Many Armors of Iron Man"]] variant cover series for {{cl|Tony Stark: Iron Man Vol 1 1}}, their numbers are shuffled around to match the sequence in which they first appeared.
| Trivia                  = * This suit is one of Iron Man's armors whose schematics are being contested by [[Damage Control (Earth-616)|Damage Control]] after Tony Stark fell into a coma since the company also operates as an archival unit for metahuman technology that belongs to missing, incapacitated or deceased individuals. While Stark commonly evaded this predicament by leaving control of his intellectual property to [[Reed Richards (Earth-616)|Reed Richards]], Reed had gone missing for a prolongued period of time when Stark became incapacitated.{{r|House of X Vol 1 1}}
| Links                   = 
}}

pages.wikitext:
{{Marvel Database:Item Template
| Image                   = Iron Man Armor Model 9 from All-New Iron Manual Vol 1 1 001.jpg
| Name                    = Iron Man Armor Model 9{{r|Iron Manual Vol 1 1}}
| Title                   = [[Iron Man Armor|Iron Man Armor Model 9]]

| Reality                 = Earth-616
| LeadDesigner            = [[Anthony Stark (Earth-616)|Tony Stark]]
| AdditionalDesigners     =

| Origin                  = Built to stop Firepower.
| Type                    = Iron Man Armor
| Dimensions              =
| Weight                  =
| Creators                = David Michelinie; Bob Layton; Mark Bright
| First                   = Iron Man Vol 1 231
| Destruction             = 

| History                 = Stark had been tinkering with this new bulkier armor behind-the-scenes before the [[Armor Wars I|first Armor Wars]] but was reluctant to use it because of it's high power capabilities. The design and color scheme was meant to be a redesign and reimagining of his [[Iron Man Armor Model 4|classic armor]]. Initially it was just a project Stark had been working on in his free-time. Later on, Stark was forced to don the armor to stop [[Firepower]] after a miserable defeat earlier in which his [[Iron Man Armor Model 7|current armor]] was destroyed by one of Firepower's missiles. Initially Stark planned to discard it after defeating Firepower; However, he continued to act as Iron Man after being inspired by his battles with Firepower. A cover story was made mentioning a fictitious Stark employee had died as Iron Man and Stark had made a new hire. A similar model was also used by Rhodes briefly.

[[File:Anthony Stark (Earth-616) from Marvel Fanfare Vol 1 45 001.jpg|thumb|left]]

While searching for the scabbard of [[Excalibur (Sword)|Excalibur]], Iron Man's armor interacted with its protective power. Combining the armor with Excalibur allowed Stark and Doom to defeat an extra-dimensional eye monster. The armor reverted to normal; Stark is only aware of the incident due to its memory chip (Merlin used a spell to remove his and Doom's memory of the events).{{r|Iron Man: Legacy of Doom Vol 1 3|4}} After being shot by [[Kathleen Dare (Earth-616)|Kathy Dare]], Tony had a bio-chip implanted in his spine. In conjunction with a special under-suit, he was able to move in the armor. He readjusted the armor's cybernetic interface after the Mars Twins' attempt to control his bio-chip. As nerve damage grew from [[Kearson DeWitt (Earth-616)|Kearson DeWitt]]'s techno-virus and mental strain, Tony switched to other armors. When [[Anthony Stark (Earth-616)|Tony Stark]] undertook Stark Resilient, he dismantled and melted a model of this armor. [[Bethany Cabe (Earth-616)|Bethany Cabe]] used this armor to battle [[Ultimo (Earth-616)|Ultimo]].

[[File:Anthony Stark (Earth-616) from Iron Man Legacy of Doom Vol 1 4 001.png|thumb|right|Powered by the scabbard of Excalibur]]

[[File:Cable and X-Force Vol 1 7 Many Armors of Iron Man Variant Textless.jpg|thumb|right]]

==Capabilities==
A Beta particle generator and solar converters became the armor's power source. As a result the armor was more powerful and faster. Fast enough to travel from [[Stuttgart|Stuttgart, Germany]], to [[Latveria]] in a matter of minutes, which would mean the suit travelled at speeds up to Mach 18, and powerful enough to hold one tank in each hand and crush them effortlessly.{{r|Iron Man: Legacy of Doom Vol 1 1}} A security chip and anti-intrusion devices were added to prevent the armor's technology from being duplicated. The cybernetic interface adapted after Stark's spinal injury. Its battle computer could track up to 60 targets simultaneously. A cybernetic probe could link to other systems. A universal translator was added to boost communications. A hydro module for underwater missions. The suit could not fly into space on Its own, needing special addons{{r|Avengers Vol 1 316}} or a [[Stark Booster Rocket|Booster Rocket]].{{r|Iron Man Vol 1 237}}

The armor retained and improved the Silver Centurion's weaponry. An {{Power|Electromagnetic Pulse Generation|EMP}} was adopted from [[Force Armor|Force]]'s usage of it. The gauntlets had a nozzle for freon or gas. An add-on could carry "titanium foam." It could also launch a "hyperwave" generator.{{r|Dragon Seed Saga}} An [[Energy Shield]] was used to protect against energy attacks. "Protected senses" acted automatically to protect Stark's sight and hearing. Stark developed {{Power|Telepathic Immunity|psi-shields}} by incorporating experimental [[Shi'ar]] technology.{{r|Warheads Vol 1 3}} The Armor could withstand 2000 degree celcius temperatures.{{r|Captain America Annual Vol 1 9}}

The suit was capable of advanced hacking, being able to override the defenses of [[Nebula (Earth-616)|Nebula]]'s spaceship,{{r|Avengers Vol 1 316}} and the super-prison [[Vault (Prison)|The Vault]].{{r|Marvel Graphic Novel Vol 1 68: Avengers: Death Trap, The Vault}}

When it was fused with [[Excalibur (Sword)|Excalibur]], the armor also featured invulnerability. All of the suit's normal functions were temporarily replaced with a magical equivalent. For example, instead of normal repulsors, it used "spell-shots." According to [[Merlyn (Earth-616)|Merlin]], the armor's power was dependent only on Stark's will.{{r|Iron Man: Legacy of Doom Vol 1 3}}

| CurrentOwner            = [[Anthony Stark (Earth-616)|Tony Stark]]
| PreviousOwners          =

| Notes                   = 
| Trivia                  = * This armor was featured as Iron Man's look for the character's appearance ahead of its comic book debut in the 1987 {{wc|macysthanksgiving|The 61st Annual Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade (1987)|Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade}} alongside other Marvel super heroes. The costume was worn by Marvel character actor [[Steve Vrattos]], who most notably portrayed Spider-Man in official events.{{cite|ref=true|url=http://www.heroesinmycloset.com/2009/12/i-love-parade-part-iii-isnt-it-iron-ic.html|title=I Love a Parade, Part III: Isn't It Iron-ic?|work=Heroes in my Closet|first=Steve|last=Vrattos|date=December 19, 2009|accessdate=January 24, 2025|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20241129142308/http://www.heroesinmycloset.com/2009/12/i-love-parade-part-iii-isnt-it-iron-ic.html|archivedate=November 29, 2024}}

| History                 = After some time out of the public eye due to burnout and scandal, Stark returned to daily life. 

Hydra attacked a gamma plant where the remaining armor had been stored; Stark and Sitwell investigated.  

[[File:Iron Man Vol 2 1 Textless.jpg|thumb|left]]
The gamma bomb's detonation had brought the Hulk to life. Hulk caused Stark's helicopter to crash. Tony suffered major injuries to his heart, and put on the armor to save his life. Feeling like he was given a second chance, Stark became active as Iron Man.

He later learned that the armor design was not flawed; it had been damaged when Rebel secretly challenged the Titanium Man.

When Tony Stark returns to [[Earth-616]], he immediatley adapts the newer [[Iron Man Armor Model 16|Renaissance Armor]].

* In 2018, the [[:Category:Many Armors of Iron Man Variants|"Many Armors of Iron Man"]] variant cover series for {{cl|Tony Stark: Iron Man Vol 1 1}} bumped up the numeric designation of several of the 20 armors it spotlighed due to the [[Iron Man Armor Model 13|Model 13]] being split into 13 and 14. One of these suits is the [[Iron Man Armor Model 37|Bleeding Edge Armor]], which was reclassified as Model 38 after having previously been officially identified as the Model 37. However, the [[Iron Man Armor Model 42|Black and Gold Armor]] retained its previously established designation of Model 42, leaving only three vacant numbers (39, 40 and 41) for the four previously-officially designated suits between it and the Bleeding Edge Armor. Due to the limited scope of the cover series making it impossible to determine the full extent of changes in numeration, the Marvel Database will prioritize the previous numbering, which stemmed from the [[Iron Manual TPB Vol 1 1|''Iron Manual'' TPB]] and [[All-New, All-Different Marvel Universe Vol 1 1|''All-New, All-Different Marvel Universe'']].
* This armor was originally designated as Model CE1 in 2008's {{cl|All-New Iron Manual Vol 1 1}} as well as the [[Iron Manual TPB Vol 1 1|''Iron Manual'' TPB]]. In 2018's [[:Category:Many Armors of Iron Man Variants|"Many Armors of Iron Man"]] variant cover series for {{cl|Tony Stark: Iron Man Vol 1 1}}, its designation was misspelled "C1E1."
| Trivia                  = * A toy version of the Prometheum Armor was produced for the Heroes Reborn ''Avengers'' line. A new one was later released under the ''Marvel Legends'' imprint.

| Creators                = Gerry Duggan; Juan Frigeri
| First                   = Invincible Iron Man Vol 5 7

| History                 = The Mark Nil was a [[Stealth Armor|stealth armor]] created by [[Anthony Stark (Earth-616)|Tony Stark]] shortly after the acquisition of [[Stark Unlimited (Earth-616)|Stark Unlimited]] by the human supremacist [[Kelvin Heng (Earth-616)|Feilong]]. He first used it to infiltrate a factory in [[Texas (State)|Texas]] where Feilong was using the technology of the company to mass-produce [[Stark Sentinel MK II|Stark Sentinels]].{{r|Invincible Iron Man Vol 5 7}}

Iron Man defaulted to the Mark Nil after Feilong issued him a cease-and-desist which forced him to turn over his then-primary suit, the [[Iron Man Armor Model 70|Model 70]]. Stark notably used the Mark Nil during his missions to subvert the campaign of mutant oppression of Feilong's allies, the think tank [[Orchis (Earth-616)|Orchis]],{{r|Invincible Iron Man Vol 5 10}} and to continue serving with the [[Avengers (Earth-616)|Avengers]].{{r|Avengers Vol 9 3|to=11}} The Mark Nil was eventually superseded by Stark's subsequent primary suit, the [[Iron Man Armor Model 72|Mysterium Armor]]. As a matter of fact, in the lead-up to the final battle against Orchis, Tony left the Mark Nil behind in the [[Hellfire Club Building (New York)|Hellfire Club]] as it burned.{{r|Invincible Iron Man Vol 5 15}} Stark later retrieved it from the burnt-down building since the suit had survived the fire.{{r|Invincible Iron Man Vol 5 19}}

| Properties              = Like any stealth armor, the Mark Nil favors undetectability and furtiveness above all else. To this end, it possesses active camouflage which renders the armor virtually {{Power|Invisibility|invisible}};{{r|Invincible Iron Man Vol 5 7}} being able to extend this effect to anything its user holds. The effectiveness of the suit's cloaking its tied to is energy expense, and it can completely cloak itself at a high-power cost. Something the armor couldn't cloak, however, was the exhaust from its propulsion systems.{{r|Invincible Iron Man Vol 5 11}} The suit also possesses what might be Van der Waals adhesion circuits similar to the [[Iron Man Armor Model 70]], which allows it to stick to vertical surfaces, mimicking [[Peter Parker (Earth-616)|Spider-Man]]'s wall-crawling.{{r|Invincible Iron Man Vol 5 7}} In terms of suit-up, the Mark Nil features an autonomic assembly process. It can fold into and out of the shape of a briefcase.{{r|Invincible Iron Man Vol 5 11}} The suit possesses the ability to open flaps from the back which reveal additional thrusters for extra thrust.{{r|Avengers Vol 9 3}} The suit can still function in it's base capacity even after taking severe damage and falling apart at the same time.{{r|Avengers Vol 9 6}}

In addition to this, the armor possesses the standard abilities of an Iron Man suit, including enhanced durability to withstand the blows from a transfigured city controlled by the [[Citysmith (Multiverse)|Citysmith]]{{r|Avengers Vol 9 4}} several blows from [[Bedivere (Twilight Court) (Earth-616)|Bedivere the Engineer]],{{r|Avengers Vol 9 9}} a blow from an empowered [[Artur (Earth-616)|Artur the King]],{{r|Avengers Vol 9 10}} strength and {{Power|Self-Propelled Flight|flight via jet boots}},{{r|Invincible Iron Man Vol 5 7}} as well as repulsor beams, high-temperature lasers,{{r|Invincible Iron Man Vol 5 10}} unibeam and stun darts,{{r|Invincible Iron Man Vol 5 3}} wrist blades{{r|Avengers Vol 9 9}} and has {{Power|Intangibility|density-shifting capabilities}}, but the armor takes severe damage after use.{{r|Avengers Vol 9 6}} However, the suit is physically weaker than a standard Iron Man armor.{{r|Invincible Iron Man Vol 5 7}}

| AlternateVersions       = 

| Notes                   = * The Mark Nil is purposefully without an official designation, something [[Anthony Stark (Earth-616)|Tony Stark]] thought was pointless especially due to the clandestine nature of the activities he was going to engage in while wearing this suit.{{r|Invincible Iron Man Vol 5 7}}
* Despite the Mark Nil's lack of numeric designation, it is very likely that it technically is the Model 71. The designation of its two successors, the [[Iron Man Armor Model 72|Mysterium]] and [[Iron Man Armor Model 73|Sentinel Buster]] suits are Model 72 and 73, respectively. This numeration omits three of the four distinct suits that Iron Man had debuted after the [[Iron Man Armor Model 70|Model 70]] outside his own comic book: the [[Iron Man Armor Model Unknown (Celestial Hulkbuster Armor)|Celestial Hulkbuster Armor]] in {{cl|Thor Vol 6 25}}, the [[Iron Man Armor Model Unknown (Dragon-Slayer Armor)|Dragon-Slayer Armor]] in {{cl|Miles Morales: Spider-Man Vol 2 7}}, and a [[Iron Man Armor Model Unknown (Space Armor)|Space Armor]] in {{cl|I Am Iron Man Vol 1 5}}. The tentatively-named [[Iron Man Armor Model 71|Model 71]] was a [[Hulkbuster Armor]] that debuted in {{cl|Hulk Vol 5 1}}, so it's possible that it would also have been omitted, making the Mark Nil the true Model 71 Armor.
| Trivia                  = * The Mark Nil almost didn't have a name in its debut issue, {{cl|Invincible Iron Man Vol 5 7}}; writer [[Gerry Duggan]] rushed to mail a note asking the dialogue to be changed in the comic to give it its name shortly before it went to print.{{cite|ref=true|url=https://twitter.com/GerryDuggan/status/1667317159259947008|title= Gerry Duggan on Twitter: "@ComicsOnline Thank you! | History                 = This armor was used by [[Anthony Stark (Earth-616)|Iron Man]] to breach into [[Transia]]n airspace and make a show of his involvement in a regional civil war where his technology had been misappropriated by the Slavic paramiliatary [[Zmaj (Earth-616)|Zmaj]] to enforce an ethnic cleansing of the country's Romani and Muslim population.

Using this armor to destroy drones sent after him,{{r|Iron Man: Legacy Vol 1 1}} its deployment doubled as a distraction while he snuck his mobile garage into the country.{{r|Iron Man: Legacy Vol 1 2}} Stark subsequently stored the suit in the mobile garage, which was in turn hidden in the barn of a local named [[Nina Demir (Earth-616)|Nina Demir]] who was aiding him. However, Nina sold out Stark to the forces of [[Victor von Doom (Earth-616)|Doctor Doom]], and [[Bram Velsing (Earth-616)|Dreadknight]] claimed the contents of the garage for his master, including this armor.{{r|Iron Man: Legacy Vol 1 3}}

The technology was subsequently incorporated by Doom into a new fleet of Doombots,{{r|Iron Man: Legacy Vol 1 4}} unaware that Stark counted on his garage's theft, and had hidden a killswitch in its components. This suit was subsequently rebuilt by Stark and kept in underground storage alongside a fleet of armor.{{r|Iron Man: Legacy Vol 1 5}}

| Properties              = ===Overview===
This suit appears to be a heavy duty version of the [[Iron Man Armor]]. In addition to the capabilities of a standard Iron Man suit, which includes enhanced durability, strength and flight, it features a repulsor blade and heat-seeking missiles that can be directed to a given target through the deployment of adhesive infrared tractors.{{r|Iron Man: Legacy Vol 1 1}}

| AlternateVersions       = 

| Notes                   = * Since {{cl|Iron Man: Legacy Vol 1 1|to=5}} is set sometime between {{cl|Iron Man Vol 3 50|to=55}}, this armor's debut is set chronologically between the [[Iron Man Armor Model 20]] and the [[Iron Man Armor Model 21]].
* This suit is not actually denominated the "Aircraft Armor." This moniker is only descriptive, since no name is provided for this armor in the comics.

{{Marvel Database:Item Template | Image = Iron Man Armor Model Unknown (Celestial Hulkbuster Armor) from Thor Vol 6 25 001.jpg | Title = [[Iron Man Armor|Iron Man Armor
(Celestial Hulkbuster Armor)]] | Name = | Aliases = | CurrentOwner = [[Anthony Stark (Earth-616)|Tony Stark]] | PreviousOwners = | AlternateOwners = | Type = Iron Man Armor | Material = | Dimensions = | Weight = | Origin = Suit of [[Iron Man Armor|powered armor]] engineered from a [[Celestials|Celestial]] corpse | Reality = Earth-616 | LeadDesigner = [[Anthony Stark (Earth-616)|Tony Stark]] | AdditionalDesigners = | PlaceOfCreation = | PlaceOfDestruction = [[Black Hand of God]] | Creators = Donny Cates; Martin Coccolo | First = Thor Vol 6 25 | Destruction = Thor Vol 6 26 | History = The origins of this armor date back to [[Knull (Earth-616)|Knull]]'s [[King in Black (Event)|invasion]] of Earth, during which [[Anthony Stark (Earth-616)|Iron Man]] used the [[Extrembiote (Earth-616)|Extrembiote]] to take control of a dead [[Celestials|Celestial]] formerly in Knull's control.{{r|King in Black Vol 1 3}} He repurposed the Celestial corpse into a wormhole generator called [[Project A.R.K.]]{{r|Hulk Vol 5 1}} After the [[Bruce Banner (Earth-616)|Hulk]] hijacked the teleporter to exit reality, nearly killing Iron Man in the process,{{r|Hulk Vol 5 1}} Tony Stark converted the corpse of the Celestial into a gigantic [[Hulkbuster Armor]].{{r|Thor Vol 6 25}} Stark deployed this suit after the Hulk was spotted at the [[Black Hand of God]] arena fighting [[Thor Odinson (Earth-616)|Thor]]. Iron Man overpowered the Hulk in the armor, but he received constant interference from [[Odin Borson (Earth-616)|Odin]] whose spirit inhabited Thor's hammer, [[Mjolnir]]. However, Banner was no longer in control of Hulk, causing Hulk's rage to go out of control and eventually unleash a massive gamma explosion, wrecking the armor.{{r|Thor Vol 6 25}}{{r|Hulk Vol 5 7}} The gamma explosion caused Thor to be transformed into an out-of-control gamma mutate. Iron Man tried to use the armor to subdue Thor, but Thor destroyed what remained of the armor.{{r|Thor Vol 6 26}} | Properties = Befitting its massive size, the armor possesses immense levels of strength and durability, though it could barely withstand a blow from Mjolnir. It also possesses various weapons, including missile batteries and guns powerful enough to hurt the Hulk and devastate a large area. On its palms are energy weapons. It's capable of interplanetary flight, traveling from [[Earth]] to the Black Hand of God in a short amount of time. The armor was also designed to absorb and withstand large amounts of gamma energy, enabling it to shield Iron Man from a gamma explosion with the power of approximately 3000 [[Gamma Bomb]]s, though the armor was heavily damaged.{{r|Thor Vol 6 25}}{{r|Hulk Vol 5 7}} | AlternateVersions = | Notes = | Trivia = | Links = }} [[Category:Destroyed Items]] [[Category:Celestial Technology]] {{DEFAULTSORT:Iron_Man_Armor_Model_071.1B|noerror}} [[Category:Anthony Stark (Earth-51156)/Items]]

pages.wikitext:
{{Marvel Database:Item Template | Image = Iron Man Armor Model Unknown (Dragon-Slayer Armor) from Carnage Reigns Omega Vol 1 1 001.jpg | Title = [[Iron Man Armor|Iron Man Armor
(Dragon-Slayer Armor)]] | Name = | Aliases = | CurrentOwner = [[Anthony Stark (Earth-616)|Tony Stark]] | PreviousOwners = | AlternateOwners = | Type = Iron Man Armor | Material = | Dimensions = | Weight = | Origin = | Reality = Earth-616 | LeadDesigner = [[Anthony Stark (Earth-616)|Tony Stark]] | AdditionalDesigners = | PlaceOfCreation = [[Bronson's Cabs Depot]], [[Jersey City]], [[New Jersey (State)|New Jersey]] | PlaceOfDestruction = | Creators = Alex Paknadel; Cody Ziglar; Julius Ohta | First = Carnage Vol 3 14 | First2 = (Shadowed)
{{cid|Miles Morales: Spider-Man Vol 2 7}}(Full appearance) | Quotation = [[Cletus Kasady (Earth-616)|You]] steal the [[Extrembiote (Earth-616)|Extrembiote]] and turn it into this monstrosity?! Who better to slay the evil dragon than a knight in titanium armor? | Speaker = [[Anthony Stark (Earth-616)|Iron Man]] | QuoteSource = Miles Morales: Spider-Man Vol 2 7 | History = The Dragon-Slayer Armor was designed by [[Anthony Stark (Earth-616)|Tony Stark]] as a contingency against the symbiotic super villain [[Cletus Kasady (Earth-616)|Cletus Kasady]] after he absorbed the [[Extrembiote (Earth-616)|Extrembiote]] off him when they last faced.{{r|Extreme Carnage Omega Vol 1 1}} Stark eventually suited up in this armor months later, when Kasady resurfaced in [[New York City]], wreaking havoc as he infected citizens via the internet, and in the process assumed a giant dragon form.{{r|Carnage Vol 3 14}} Stark intercepted Kasady's fight with [[Miles Morales (Earth-1610)|Spider-Man]] and his reluctant allies, the [[New York City Police Department (Earth-616)|NYPD]]'s [[Cape Killers (Earth-616)|Cape Killers]]. Iron Man drained his suit's power cells dealing a seemingly definitive attack, and he had Spider-Man use his venom blast to recharge it. However, Kasady hadn't been taken out, and he critically injured Spider-Man. Stark injected him with a nanite cluster to speed up his recovery, which manifested itself as a brand-new [[Iron Spider Armor]].{{r|Miles Morales: Spider-Man Vol 1 7}} Iron Man reconverged with Spider-Man and the Cape Killers to lay out his plan; to detonate an EMP from within Kasady, so he needed them to cut away enough of the villain's symbiote matter for him to punch through his armor. The plan was derailed when Kasady made bystanders go berserk, and also convened a trio of his followers, whom he had assimilated into stolen symbiote-infused Iron Man suits. After Kasady set out to escape the Earth to search for the Carnage symbiote in space, Iron Man had Spider-Man distract him long enough while he charged the EMP. Stark rammed himself into Kasady at full speed and detonated the attack. It fried his armor's sytems, but it disintegrated Kasady's Extrembiote dragon form and freed all the citizens under his thrall.{{r|Carnage Reigns Omega Vol 1 1}} | Properties = This suit possesses the standard abilities of an Iron Man Armor. It provides its user with superhuman strength and durability, as well as the ability to fly via boot jets. Its systems are run by the A.I. [[B.O.S.S. (Earth-616)|B.O.S.S.]], and it features communication and scanning capabilities.{{r|Miles Morales: Spider-Man Vol 2 7}} In addition to firing blasts, the Dragon-Slayer's repulsor modules can also conjure up hard-light constructs, namely a lance and a shield. The armor can also fire a sonic blast, and its strongest weapon is an EMP, which is so powerful it could disintegrate the [[Extrembiote (Earth-616)|Extrembiote]] and defeat [[Cletus Kasady (Earth-616)|Cletus Kasady]] after he had assimilated a [[Stark Sentinel MK II|Stark Sentinel]], but at the cost of the armor's internal systems being fried. The armor could self-repair from lesser damage,{{r|Carnage Reigns Omega Vol 1 1}} and it can also deliver a cluster of nanites which were once used on [[Miles Morales (Earth-1610)|Spider-Man]] to heal his injuries, and they formed around him a new [[Iron Spider Armor]].{{r|Miles Morales: Spider-Man Vol 2 7}} | AlternateVersions = | Notes = | Trivia = | Links = }} {{DEFAULTSORT:Iron_Man_Armor_Model_071.1F|noerror}}

pages.title: Iron Man Armor Model Unknown (Explorer Armor)
pages.wikitext:
{{Marvel Database:Item Template | Image = Iron Man Armor Model Unknown (Explorer Armor) from Iron Man Vol 5 25 001.jpg | Title = [[Iron Man Armor|Iron Man Armor
(Explorer Armor)]] | Name = | Aliases = | CurrentOwner = [[Anthony Stark (Earth-616)|Tony Stark]] | PreviousOwners = | AlternateOwners = | Type = Iron Man Armor | Material = | Dimensions = | Weight = | Origin = Suit of [[Iron Man Armor|powered armor]] | Reality = Earth-616 | LeadDesigner = [[Anthony Stark (Earth-616)|Tony Stark]] | AdditionalDesigners = | PlaceOfCreation = | PlaceOfDestruction = | Creators = Murewa Ayodele; Dotun Akande | First = Iron Man Vol 5 25 | History = The Explorer Armor was a suit designed by [[Anthony Stark (Earth-616)|Tony Stark]] for exploration of uncharted territories with extensive life-support capabilities. He used it to venture into [[Jotunheim]] in the search for [[Thor Odinson (Earth-616)|Thor]] following a prolonged and unexplained absence from [[Earth]]. During this time, Thor was undergoing an identity crisis after he lost the ability to wield his hammer, [[Mjolnir]], and had simply retreated into Jotunheim on his own volition.{{r|Iron Man Vol 5 25}} | Properties = ===Overview=== Although not particularly one of [[Anthony Stark (Earth-616)|Tony Stark]]'s strongest suits, the Explorer Armor has impressive life support capabilities, and it is ideal for the exploration of unfamiliar destinations.{{cite|ref=true|url=https://twitter.com/ayodelemurewa/status/1593122929637982210|title=Murewa Ayodele on Twitter: "@MiamiCapitalist @Dotun_Ak Hi. ...|work=Twitter|first=Murewa|last=Ayodele|date=17 November 2022|accessdate=25 December 2022|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20221226024055/https://twitter.com/ayodelemurewa/status/1593122929637982210|archivedate=25 December 2022}} When Iron Man ventured into [[Jotunheim]], it managed to shield him from temperatures of -157 °F (-105 °C) for over eight days with only signs of mild discomfort, administering nutrients and water through intravenous therapy. The armor can also extract nutrients from external sources using tubes that extend from the tips of its fingers. Additionally, the suit possesses the standard abilities of a regular Iron Man Armor, including flight, enhanced strength, increased durability, repulsor blasts and unibeam. It can also generate holographic shields, and has displayed limited shape-shifting functions, turning his boots into clamps.{{r|Iron Man Vol 5 25}} Because the armor's primary function is life support, every other task it can perform at a basic level. For instance, the suit possesses camouflage, but it only covers solid colors.{{cite|ref=true|url=https://twitter.com/ayodelemurewa/status/1593274148897390597|title=Murewa Ayodele on Twitter: "@MiamiCapitalist @Dotun_Ak It ...|work=Twitter|first=Murewa|last=Ayodele|date=17 November 2022|accessdate=25 December 2022|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20221226024315/https://twitter.com/ayodelemurewa/status/1593274148897390597|archivedate=25 December 2022}} When it comes to the Explorer Armor's energy systems, the suit relies on both an [[Arc Reactor|arc reactor]] and solar radiation to recharge, and it is imperative for it to never run out of battery. It turns black to absorb solar radiation better, and it turns white when fully charged.{{cite|ref=true|url=https://twitter.com/ayodelemurewa/status/1593125415576817664|title=Murewa Ayodele on Twitter: "@MiamiCapitalist @Dotun_Ak The...|work=Twitter|first=Murewa|last=Ayodele|date=17 November 2022|accessdate=25 December 2022|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20221226113545/https://twitter.com/ayodelemurewa/status/1593125415576817664|archivedate=26 December 2022}} The suit is outfitted with a specialty A.I. called [[B.R.I.A.N. (Earth-616)|B.R.I.A.N.]],{{r|Iron Man Vol 5 25}} which specializes in life support.{{cite|ref=true|url=https://twitter.com/ayodelemurewa/status/1593128600835788800|title=Murewa Ayodele on Twitter: "@MiamiCapitalist @Dotun_Ak ...|work=Twitter|first=Murewa|last=Ayodele|date=17 November 2022|accessdate=25 December 2022|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20221226113545/https://twitter.com/ayodelemurewa/status/1593128600835788800|archivedate=26 December 2022}} | AlternateVersions = | Notes = * This armor debuted in the back-up story "Daddy's Boys" in {{cl|Iron Man Vol 5 25}}. Its writer [[Murewa Ayodele]], revealed most of the armor's functions on social media.{{cite|ref=true|url=https://twitter.com/ayodelemurewa/status/1593122929637982210|title=Murewa Ayodele on Twitter: "@MiamiCapitalist @Dotun_Ak Hi. ...|work=Twitter|first=Murewa|last=Ayodele|date=17 November 2022|accessdate=25 December 2022|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20221226024055/https://twitter.com/ayodelemurewa/status/1593122929637982210|archivedate=25 December 2022}} * Since "Daddy's Boys" is set during the period of time that [[Thor Odinson (Earth-616)|Thor]] was unworthy of [[Mjolnir]] and [[Jane Foster (Earth-616)|Jane Foster]] was wielding it, the Explorer Armor's debut is set chronologically between the [[Iron Man Armor Model 50|Endo-Sym]] and the [[Iron Man Armor Model 51|Model-Prime Armor]]. | Trivia = * The name of the Explorer Armor's A.I., B.R.I.A.N., is a homage to Iron Man writer [[Brian Michael Bendis]].{{cite|ref=true|url=https://twitter.com/ayodelemurewa/status/1593128600835788800|title=Murewa Ayodele on Twitter: "@MiamiCapitalist @Dotun_Ak ...|work=Twitter|first=Murewa|last=Ayodele|date=17 November 2022|accessdate=25 December 2022|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20221226113545/https://twitter.com/ayodelemurewa/status/1593128600835788800|archivedate=26 December 2022}} * [[Murewa Ayodele]] loves the Explorer Armor because it allows [[Anthony Stark (Earth-616)|Iron Man]] to "travel and fill his curiosity -- to go on adventures and be a scientist. Many Marvel heroes are great fighters, Explorer Armor makes him stand out as the curious scientist that he is."{{cite|ref=true|url=https://twitter.com/ayodelemurewa/status/1685422222528167936|title=Murewa Ayodele on X: @DotunAk Iron Man is a curious soul. I love an ...|work=X|first=Murewa|last=Ayodele|date=29 July, 2023|accessdate=April 9, 2024|archiveurl=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/nfm8m|archivedate=April 9, 2024}} | Links = }} {{DEFAULTSORT:Iron_Man_Armor_Model_050.1A|noerror}}

When a time-displaced teenager [[Anthony Stark (Earth-96020)|Tony Stark]] was brought into the present by the [[Avengers (Earth-616)|Avengers]] to help them defeat his brainwashed future self, they broke into the Arctic bunker, where they were ambushed by Iron Man. pages.title: Iron Man Armor Model Unknown (Shogun Armor)
pages.wikitext:
{{Marvel Database:Item Template | Image = Iron Man Armor Model Unknown (Shogun Armor) from I Am Iron Man Vol 1 3 001.jpg | Title = [[Iron Man Armor|Iron Man Armor
(Shogun Armor)]] | Name = | Aliases = | CurrentOwner = [[Anthony Stark (Earth-616)|Tony Stark]] | PreviousOwners = | AlternateOwners = | Type = Iron Man Armor | Material = | Dimensions = | Weight = | Origin = Suit of [[Iron Man Armor|powered armor]] | Reality = Earth-616 | LeadDesigner = [[Anthony Stark (Earth-616)|Tony Stark]] | AdditionalDesigners = | PlaceOfCreation = | PlaceOfDestruction = | Creators = Murewa Ayodele; Dotun Akande | First = I Am Iron Man Vol 1 3 | History = The Shogun Armor was a suit used by [[Anthony Stark (Earth-616)|Iron Man]] to infiltrate [[Mojoworld]] and reenact the play-pretend scenario of a kid named [[Character Index/B#Bobby|Bobby]], whose mother had been kidnapped from [[Earth]] by [[Mojo (Mojoverse)|Mojo]] during play time. Back home, Bobby had crafted a scenario in which his mother was kidnapped by an Oni Queen and he was her savior, the Iron Shogun, but she deviated from his plot during the hero's confrontation against the Oni Queen, lunging at him to tickle him. [[File:Anthony Stark (Earth-616) from I Am Iron Man Vol 1 3 001.jpg|thumb|left|Brandishing his katanas]] Iron Man ventured into Mojoworld alongisde [[James Rhodes (Earth-616)|War Machine]] and played the starring role as he followed Bobby's script, brought to life by Mojo using holograms and robot onis, counting on Bobby's mother to know to break away from the script at the same moment of the story as she did back home. When Tony faced the robot [[Oni Queen (Mojoverse)|Oni Queen]], Bobby's mother similarly leapt at him. War Machine, who had played the supporting role of the "War Monger," provided cover from Mojo's robots as Iron Man shed away the Shogun Armor, which transfigured into a escape pod for Bobby's mother. Afterward, Iron Man and War Machine escorted the escape pod back to Earth and reunited Bobby with his mother.{{r|I Am Iron Man Vol 1 3}} | Properties = ===Overview=== The Shogun Armor appears to possess the standard capabilities of an Iron Man suit, including enhanced durability, strength and flight. Instead of [[Glossary:Repulsor|repulsor]] beams, this armor's main weapon is a pair of katanas, which ignite with red plasma when they are unsheathed. The armor can also transfigure itself flying platform with an energy field casing meant to be used as an escape pod.{{r|I Am Iron Man Vol 1 3}} | AlternateVersions = | Notes = * Since {{cl|I Am Iron Man Vol 1 3}} is set during [[Kurt Busiek]]'s run in {{cl|Iron Man Vol 3}}, the Shogun Armor's debut is set chronologically between the [[Iron Man Armor Model 16|Heroes Return]] and the [[Iron Man Armor Model 19|S.K.I.N. Armor]]. * This armor's faceplate is derivative of the helmet of the [[Iron Man Armor Model 70]], an armor that debuted chronologically years after the Shogun Armor in-universe. * Although [[James Rhodes (Earth-616)|Jim Rhodes]] similarly adopts a samurai-ized version of his super hero alias in ''I Am Iron Man'' #3, his "War Monger" suit doesn't appear to be an actual functioning battlesuit. Unlike Iron Man, who fights Mojo's oni robots as the Iron Shogun, War Machine takes off his War Monger costume to wage battle. | Trivia = * The Shogun Armor was inspired by [[Anthony Stark (Earth-616)|Iron Man]]'s [[Iron Man Armor Model 51|Model-Prime Armor]] shapeshifting into samurai-esque configuration in {{cl|Invincible Iron Man Vol 3 4}}. The animated series ''{{WP|Samurai Jack}}'' and samurai anime in general "helped too."{{cite|ref=true|url=https://twitter.com/ayodelemurewa/status/1658026261334175744|title=Murewa Ayodele on X: "The samurai iteration of Model Prime armor was a...|work=X|first=Murewa|last=Ayodele|date=May 15, 2023|accessdate=April 20, 2024|archiveurl=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/j2IC2|archivedate=April 9, 2024}} | Links = }} {{DEFAULTSORT:Iron_Man_Armor_Model_016.1A|noerror}}

(Subterranean Armor)]] | Name = | Aliases = Subterranean Armor{{r|Iron Man: Legacy Vol 1 2}} | CurrentOwner = [[Anthony Stark (Earth-616)|Tony Stark]] | PreviousOwners = | AlternateOwners = | Type = Iron Man Armor | Material = | Dimensions = | Weight = | Origin = Suit of [[Iron Man Armor|powered armor]] | Reality = Earth-616 | LeadDesigner = [[Anthony Stark (Earth-616)|Tony Stark]] | AdditionalDesigners = | PlaceOfCreation = | PlaceOfDestruction = | Creators = Fred Van Lente; Steve Kurth | First = Iron Man: Legacy Vol 1 2 | History = [[File:Anthony Stark (Earth-616) from Iron Man Legacy Vol 1 2 001.jpg|thumb|left]] The Subterranean Armor was used by [[Anthony Stark (Earth-616)|Iron Man]] when he involved himself in a [[Transia]]n civil war to stop the ethnic cleansing of the country's Romani and Muslim population being commited by the Slavic paramiliatary [[Zmaj (Earth-616)|Zmaj]]. Since the Zmaj's remote-piloted "Iron Men" moved through underground mines to avoid detection from orbit, Stark used the Subtearranean Armor to mimic their M.O. and intercept one of their assaults on civilians. Iron Man managed to destroy several of the "Iron Men" until one of them distracted him with a holographic decoy of a child in peril, following up the distraction with a devastating attack that destroyed the Subterranean Armor.{{r|Iron Man: Legacy Vol 1 2}} The suit was subsequently rebuilt by Stark and kept in underground storage alongside a fleet of armor.{{r|Iron Man: Legacy Vol 1 5}} | Properties = ===Overview=== This suit appears to be a heavy duty version of the [[Iron Man Armor]]. In addition to the capabilities of a standard Iron Man suit, which includes enhanced durability, strength, flight and a unibeam, the Subterranean Armor's lower arms can shapeshift into powerful drills. It can also generate a localized magnetosphere.{{r|Iron Man: Legacy Vol 1 2}} | AlternateVersions = | Notes = * Since {{cl|Iron Man: Legacy Vol 1 1|to=5}} is set sometime between {{cl|Iron Man Vol 3 50|to=55}}, this armor's debut is set chronologically between the [[Iron Man Armor Model 20]] and the [[Iron Man Armor Model 21]]. | Links = }} {{DEFAULTSORT:Iron_Man_Armor_Model_020.1B|noerror}}

pages.title: Iron Man Armor Model Unknown (Temporal Armor)
pages.wikitext:
{{Marvel Database:Item Template | Image = Iron Man Armor Model Unknown (Temporal Armor) from Iron Man Kiss and Kill Vol 1 1 002.jpg | Title = [[Iron Man Armor|Iron Man Armor
(Temporal Armor)]] | Name = | Aliases = "Cold War Armor"{{r|Iron Man: Kiss and Kill Vol 1 1}} | CurrentOwner = [[Anthony Stark (Earth-616)|Tony Stark]] | PreviousOwners = | AlternateOwners = | Type = Iron Man Armor | Material = | Dimensions = | Weight = | Origin = Suit of [[Iron Man Armor|powered armor]] | Reality = Earth-616 | LeadDesigner = [[Anthony Stark (Earth-616)|Tony Stark]] | AdditionalDesigners = [[Victor von Doom (Earth-616)|Doctor Doom]] | PlaceOfCreation = | PlaceOfDestruction = | Creators = Joe Ahearne; Brian Ching | First = Iron Man: Kiss and Kill Vol 1 1 | Quotation = Let's just say the weaponry in '''this model''' was developed against my '''better judgment.''' | Speaker = [[Anthony Stark (Earth-616)|Iron Man]] | QuoteSource = Iron Man: Kiss and Kill Vol 1 1 | History = Designed with inspiration from [[Victor von Doom (Earth-616)|Doctor Doom]]'s [[Time Platform]], [[Anthony Stark (Earth-616)|Tony Stark]] deemed the Temporal Armor too dangerous. He decommissioned and buried the suit with a self-destruct protocol built in before its potentially devastating weaponry could be used. [[Sunset Bain (Earth-616)|Sunset Bain]] eventually retrieved the armor. Since Tony's brainwave signature was required to make it function, she adopted the identity of "Dr. Tessa Nubin," pretending to be a [[Georgia (Country)|Georgian]] illegal arms dealer in possession of the suit in order to lure Stark to it. [[File:Iron Man Armor Model Unknown (Temporal Armor) from Iron Man Kiss and Kill Vol 1 1 001.jpg|thumb|left|Schematics]] After almost two months of preparation, Stark eventually infiltrated "Dr. Nubin"'s operations as a client, under his own undercover identity of Professor Traski. Aware of Stark's deception, Bain restrained him and used a modified [[Slave Discs|Slave Disc]] to immobilize him as she forced the armor on him. Bain intended to have the armor flown as a missile, using its time-travelling abilities to hit her target, [[Avengers Mansion]], circa the team's formation. [[Natalia Romanova (Earth-616)|Black Widow]], who had assisted Stark with his infiltration, grappled to the suit mid-flight. After the armor traveled to the past, Natasha managed to feed him a pill through his mouth slit which triggered a heart attack, breaking the armor's neural connection and disarming its fusion charges. The armor crashed into Avengers Mansion, but Natasha steered it harmlessly past the original [[Avengers (Earth-616)|Avengers]] until the suit opened another portal into the present, after which she resuscitated Tony.{{r|Iron Man: Kiss and Kill Vol 1 1}} | Properties = [[File:Anthony Stark (Earth-616) from Iron Man Kiss and Kill Vol 1 1 006.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Temporal Port activating]] ===Overview=== The Temporal Armor appears to possess the standard abilities of a regular Iron Man Armor, including flight, enhanced strength, increased durability, repulsor blasts and unibeam. Its primary function is to double as a [[Glossary:Time Travel|time machine]]. Using a mechanism derived from [[Victor von Doom (Earth-616)|Doctor Doom]]'s [[Time Platform]], the armor can open a "Temporal Port" in front of its flight path. Other weaponry includes devastating fusion charges. The suit requires [[Anthony Stark (Earth-616)|Tony Stark]]'s brainwave signature to operate, although Stark himself believed its encryption could be broken with enough work. [[Sunset Bain (Earth-616)|Sunset Bain]] estimated that it would take years to bypass this encryption system.{{r|Iron Man: Kiss and Kill Vol 1 1}} | AlternateVersions = | Notes = * Although released in June 2010, this armor's debut in the story "Iron Widow" in {{cl|Iron Man: Kiss and Kill Vol 1 1}} takes place before 2008's ''[[Secret Invasion (Event)|Secret Invasion]]'' due to the appearance of [[Stark Enterprises (Earth-616)|Stark Enterprises]], which collapsed during the event. If "Iron Widow" takes place around the same time as the other story in the issue, "Glitch," the story would be chronologically set even before ''[[Civil War (Event)|Civil War]]''. * The Temporal Armor reutilizes the design of the [[Iron Man Armor Model 29|Iron Man Armor Model 29]], the Extremis Armor, almost completely, with the exception of its helmet resembling that of the [[Iron Man Armor MK III (Earth-199999)|Iron Man Armor MK III]] from the [[Earth-199999|Marvel Cinematic Universe]]. Due to this near-identical resemblance, the Temporal Armor could be considered a subset of the Model 29. | Trivia = | Links = }} {{DEFAULTSORT:Iron_Man_Armor_Model_029.1A|noerror}} [[Category:Time Travel]] [[Category:Anthony Stark (Earth-616)/Items]] [[Category:Iron Man Armor]]

Gage; Donald Mustard; Sergio Dávila | First = Fortnite X Marvel: Zero War Vol 1 5 | Quotation = I mean, it's not my [[Hulkbuster Armor|'''Hulkbuster''']] suit, but that's kind of specifically for busting [[Bruce Banner (Earth-616)|Hulks]]. This stuff '''defies the laws of physics.''' I can't wait to take it [[Earth-616|back home]]. | Speaker = [[Anthony Stark (Earth-616)|Iron Man]] | QuoteSource = Fortnite X Marvel: Zero War Vol 1 5 | History = The Iron Man Zero was designed by [[w:c:Fortnite:The Seven|The Seven]]'s [[w:c:Fortnite:The Scientist|Scientist]] alongside [[Anthony Stark (Earth-616)|Tony Stark]] for the later to use it in the final battle of the Zero War against the [[w:c:Fortnite:Imagined Order|Imagined Order]]. It was of great use until it was disabled by a blast from [[w:c:Fortnite:Geno|Geno]] in the final push of the battle. Stark himself survived the blast undamaged, but the other heroes had to destroy the crystals of the [[w:c:Fortnite:The Collider|The Collider]] without him. As no technology from [[w:c:Fortnite:Reality Zero|Reality Zero]] was allowed leave, Stark had to leave the remains of the Iron Man Zero behind when he returned [[Earth-616|home]].{{r|Fortnite X Marvel: Zero War Vol 1 5}} | Properties = This armor was designed has a fusion between The Seven's and Iron Man's armors and was purely made for combat. It was designed to be worn over the [[Iron Man Armor Model 70|Model 70]], and appeared to improve upon the standard Iron Man Armor abilities of flight, repulsor blasts, and enhanced strength and durability. Stark himself noted that this was an incredibly powerful armor, as it "defies the laws of physics."{{r|Fortnite X Marvel: Zero War Vol 1 5}} The armor is also equipped with a wrist-mounted blade for combat.{{r|Fortnite|; Zero War Frontlines Loading Screen}} As the armor is based on those used by the members of [[w:c:Fortnite:The Seven|The Seven]] and was designed by [[w:c:Fortnite:The Scientist|The Scientist]] himself, it can be assumed to possess most of the standard functionalities and equipment associated with Seven armor. These include an energy shield, a sealed environment capable of protecting the user from extremely hazardous conditions such as [[w:c:Fortnite:The Loop|The Loop]], the vacuum of space, and even [[w:c:Fortnite:The Nothing|The Nothing]] itself, as well as a highly advanced [[w:c:fortnite:AMIE|AI assistant]], self-repair systems for minor damage, an advanced cloaking system capable of concealing body heat, sound, and energy signatures,{{r|Fortnite X Marvel: Zero War Vol 1 1}} a stasis function designed to preserve the user's life in critical situations, {{r|Fortnite X Marvel: Zero War Vol 1 3}} and technology allowing travel across realities through rifts. While direct hit from the "[[Thanos (Earth-616)|Thanos]]-level" [[w:c:Fortnite:Geno|Geno]] incapacited the armor without destroying it, it left its user and the Model 70 relatively unharmed, showing the apparent upper limits of the Iron Man Zero's durability.{{r|Fortnite X Marvel: Zero War Vol 1 5}} | AlternateVersions = | Notes = | Trivia = | Links = }} {{DEFAULTSORT:Iron_Man_Armor_Model_071.1D|noerror}}

The armor was specially designed by Tony Stark when he wanted to retire as Iron Man. He built it to be used by others so they could fight crime in his place.{{r|Iron Man (2010 animated series) Season 1 1}}

Tony brought the armor to [[Japan]] for testing, but it was stolen by the Zodiac. They were used by [[Ho Yinsen (Earth-101001)|Ho Yinsen]] against Tony. Tony fought Yinsen in their respective armor, but Yinsen dies in a battle with the [[Iron Man Sigma]] (robots created by Yinsen and controlled by [[Zodiac (Earth-101001)|Zodiac]]). Afterwards, he took the armor back to the [[United States of America]] for safekeeping.{{r|Iron Man (2010 animated series) Season 1 1}}

==Armaments==
* Repulsor Ray
* Unibeam
* Repulsor Boot Jets
* Missile Launchers

==Other==
* Heads Up Display
* Communication Systems

| Weight                  = 1775 lbs.

| History                 = This model is an improvement from the test models of [[Antonio Stark (Earth-1610)|Tony Stark]]'s youth. It was used by Stark during his first missions with the Ultimates, built after the Chitauri Invasion. An older "clunker" is held in reserve.

It needs a full crew to help Tony Stark to suit up as well to monitor it.

Stark started using an upgraded version of this armor after the Chitauri invasion, but stopped using it during the Ultimatum event, where he returned to the previous version of the Iron Tech armor.

This upgraded version is stated to be way more stable than the previous armor. It has been used in combat against the Kree,{{r|Ultimate Secret Vol 1 4}} Thor,{{r|Ultimates 2 Vol 1 5}} and a Venom-possessed Spider-Man.{{r|Ultimate Spider-Man Vol 1 126}} It has also been used during rescue missions, for example, to save an European submarine.

After the Ultimatum downgrade, the armor was heavily damaged during a battle with the [[Ghost (Earth-1610)|Ghost]] and later finished off against [[Howard Stark Sr. (Earth-1610)|Howard Stark]]'s forces. Tony then decided to use a more aerodynamic and compact armor.

==Capabilities==
A special liquid helps insulate the wearer.

Repulsors and lasers can be fired from the palm ports.

The deflector dish can emit energies, but is primarily used for a force field that can expand to a 500-meter radius.

A smaller "bubble" of force can be used for capture and containment.

Neuroscramblers can temporarily disable others.

The suit is designed for "light negation", a form of cloaking.

''Flashbulbs'' can be launched to provide extra illumination and sensor array.

A satellite array helps with recharging.

| CurrentOwner            = [[Antonio Stark (Earth-1610)|Tony Stark]]
| PreviousOwners          = 

| Notes                   = 

* The Iron Tech armor was noted as upgraded from its earlier version in {{cl|Ultimates 2 Vol 1 2}}.
* There is no explanation as to why Stark stopped using the upgraded version and returned to the previous one after the [[Liberators (Earth-1610)|Liberators]]' attack. However, it could be assumed that the upgraded armor was destroyed by the Liberators, and since Ultron stole the next one almost immediately after its first appearance, Tony didn't have time to build a new one.

| First                   = Empyre Vol 1 4

| History                 = During the [[Cotati]]'s invasion of [[Earth]], [[Anthony Stark (Earth-616)|Tony Stark]] secluded himself at [[Avengers Mountain]] to work on countermeasures against the Cotati's plant-controlling powers.{{r|Empyre Vol 1 3}} The end result as an [[Iron Man]]-like suit of armor that he designed for [[Reed Richards (Earth-616)|Mister Fantastic]], leader of the [[Fantastic Four (Earth-616)|Fantastic Four]].{{r|Empyre Vol 1 4}}

Mister Fantastic donned the armor for the final confrontation against the Cotati's leader [[Sequoia (Earth-616)|Quoi]] in [[Wakanda]], where he planned to plant a seed for a [[Death Blossom]] in the [[Vibranium]]-enriched soil of the [[Mena Ngai|Great Mound]].{{r|Empyre Vol 1 5}} Mister Fantastic joined the fight against Quoi minutes before the Death Blossom flowered, resulting in a fight that saw the destruction of the Death Blossom and the defeat of the Cotati.{{r|Empyre Vol 1 6}}

Following the Cotati's invasion, Mister Fantastic intended to set his armor aside as a Christmas gift for his son [[Franklin Richards (Earth-616)|Franklin]]. When the abstract entity known as the [[Griever at the End of All Things (Multiverse)|Griever at the End of All Things]] returned and attacked the Fantastic Four, Reed gave Franklin the suit as part of a plan to defeat their enemy. Franklin remotely piloted the suit to confront the Griever, luring her into [[4 Yancy Street]]. Reed then collapsed the different pocket dimensions within the building, causing it to fold into itself in, an attempt to trap the Griever.{{r|Fantastic Four Vol 6 27}} While the building was subsequently restored, Reed didn't manage to restore every dimension that had been folded into the building, causing the loss of a portion of the team's equipment and belongings.{{r|Fantastic Four Vol 6 29}} Whether Mister Fantastic's armor was one of the pieces of equipment lost or not is unknown.

==Properties==
===Overview===
This suit appears to possess the standard abilities of a regular Iron Man Armor, including flight and increased durability. The armor was also designed to conform to Mister Fantastic's elastic powers, and its main feature is the ability to emit through its gauntlets sonic frequencies capable of disrupting the Cotati's communication with plants based on principles of bioacoustics.{{r|Empyre Vol 1 6}} The suit can also be piloted remotely via a VR headset and control console.{{r|Fantastic Four Vol 6 27}}

Tony used the armor to rescue the [[Avengers (Earth-12041)|Avengers]] and defeat [[Justin Hammer (Earth-12041)|Justin Hammer]]'s dinosaur servants. This armor was made of a high density crystalline obsidian allowing it repel bullets. The armor also made use of vines that had been vulcanised to match the tensile strength of steel, allowing Stark to move like he does in his regular armor. The vines around the wrists had rocks attached to them that Tony used as melee weapons.

| History                 = '''Silver Centurion Armor''' is a variation of the Iron Man Armor. This armor made its first appearance in ''Whiplash''. Tony was concerned about where his enemies get their high tech weapons so he began building another suit, one that was more powerful. When the villain [[Marco Scarlotti (Earth-904913)|Whiplash]] threatened his friends and easily took down his standard suit, he put his new armor on and engaged him. The battle played out with both Tony and Whiplash evenly matched. He had trouble at first, but Iron Man won by blasting Whiplash into a power station that blew up his robotic arm.{{r|Iron Man: Armored Adventures Season 1 5}}

It was later seen in ''Don't Worry, Be Happy'' when Tony lowered it from his armory to retrieve his armor that was abandoned.{{r|Iron Man: Armored Adventures Season 1 22}}

| Properties           =
The Silver Centurion armor is stronger and more powerful than the standard armor. Its capabilities are:
*'''Superhuman Strength:''' The Silver Centurion is equipped with larger gauntlets to increase the armor's own strength.
*'''Enhanced Durability:''' The suit protects against damage and it could better withstand [[Whiplash|Whiplash's]] electric whips without getting its circuits fried.
*'''Flight:''' It flies through the use of boot jet thrusters.
*'''Repulsors:''' Its repulsors are stronger than the standard armor.
*'''Unibeam:''' The unibeam is much more powerful than the standard armor.

| History                 = The '''Space Armor''' is a space variation of the Iron Man suit. The Space Armor made its debut in Fun With'' ''Lasers. When [[Anthony Stark (Earth-904913)|Tony Stark]] learns that the [[Arthur Parks (Earth-904913)|Living Laser]] has returned and hijacked a space station that he could use to destroy entire cities, he flew into space to stop him, but only after taking a little detour with [[Strategic Hazard Intervention, Espionage Logistics Directorate (Earth-904913)|S.H.I.E.L.D.]] He entered the station and was taken by surprise by the Laser, he took some major punishment which damaged his oxygen reserves and Iron Man accidentally blew a big hole in the hangar which shot him into space. After barely finding a way to get back inside, he fought the Living Laser again, but Iron Man played on his inferiority complex to get him to enter the telescope he was going to use to destroy New York, which Iron Man had used to trap the Living Laser inside using its own mirrors.{{r|Iron Man: Armored Adventures Season 1 16}}

The Space armor design was later used to create the [[Force Armor (Earth-904913)|Force Armor]].{{r|Iron Man: Armored Adventures Season 2 5}}

Stark used his Space Armor in Doomsday to calibrate the settings of a satellite in space that he made to track down [[Makluan]] energy signatures in the world in order to find [[Gene Khan (Earth-904913)|Mandarin]].{{r|Iron Man: Armored Adventures Season 2 24}}

Howard Stark equipped himself with the Space Armor in The'' ''Makluan'' ''Invasion'' ''Part'' ''2'': ''Unite! to attach his new quantum field neutralizer cannon to the Stark satellite, which will be used to temporarily disable the [[Mandarins Rings|Makluan Rings]]. Tony used his Extremis to target the beam directly at the rings.{{r|Iron Man: Armored Adventures Season 2 26}}

| Properties              = The Space Armor has the following capabilities:
*'''Superhuman Strength:''' It's just as strong as the standard armor. The armor increases the wearer's strength immensely to allow him to lift massive weights without much effort.
*'''Enhanced Durability:''' It is extremely resistant against all types of punishment and can even completely resist the harsh conditions of outer space.
*'''Flight:''' The armor has propulsion jets in the boots to fly in the air.
*'''Repulsor Gauntlets:''' They have many functions.
**'''Repulsors: '''It can shoot concussive blasts from the palms.
**'''Computer Hacking:''' The gauntlets can plug into a computer using wires from its repulsors.
*'''Unibeam:''' The power source on the chest can produce a powerful concussive beam that can overwhelm almost anything in its path.
*'''Magnetic Manipulation:''' The armor can manipulate magnetic fields to attract small metal objects.
*'''Expanded Propulsion System:''' The armor has rockets on its back that allow the armor to fly itself into space in just a few minutes.
*'''Greater Life Support:''' It contains extended life support capabilities for operation in space.
*If the oxygen reserves are damaged while the pilot is in space, the pilot will have seconds of air left until imminent death.

| First                   = Iron Man: Armored Adventures Season 1 12

| History                 = The '''Stealth Armor''' is a variation of the Iron Man suit. [[Anthony Stark (Earth-904913)|Tony Stark]] used this armor in ''Field Trip'' to sneak into [[Stark Tower]] and investigate his father's vault, but its power cells went dead while he was still in the building. After Tony barely managed to get out without getting arrested, he and his friends arranged a school field trip to find, repair, and get the Stealth armor out of the building. It has a lot of setbacks, but the plan was a success and they got it out without getting into serious trouble.{{r|Iron Man: Armored Adventures Season 1 8}}

He used the Stealth armor again in ''Panther's Prey'' to follow an [[Advanced Idea Mechanics (Earth-904913)|A.I.M.]] hover transport and keep an eye out for the [[T'Challa (Earth-904913)|Black Panther]] without being seen. However, they were both discovered and the transport started shooting at them, resulting in the Panther being hurt and brought back to [[Armory|The Armory]] for recovery.{{r|Iron Man: Armored Adventures Season 1 15}}

The armor was shown exploding by an overload in the season one finale, ''Tales of Suspense Part 1.''{{r|Iron Man: Armored Adventures Season 1 25}}

Iron Man later used a rebuilt Stealth armor to follow the [[Ghost (Earth-904913)|Ghost]] when he stole his armor specs from the Armory in ''Ghost in the Machine''. But he failed and the Ghost got away. He later found him and, enraged, beat him down. But Ghost delivers an ultimatum, destroy him and everyone knows Iron Man's true identity, which he is planning to do once he turns 18 and takes over Stark International. Iron Man lets him go.{{r|Iron Man: Armored Adventures Season 2 4}}

The Stealth Armor designs are used in creation of the [[Shockwave Armor (Earth-904913)|Shockwave Armor]] used by one of the [[Guardsmen (Earth-904913)|Guardsmen]].{{r|Iron Man: Armored Adventures Season 2 5}}

After his first scuffle with [[Justin Hammer (Earth-904913)|Titanium Man]], he upgrades the Stealth Armor to be as powerful as the Mark II armor.

[[Patricia Potts (Earth-904913)|Pepper Potts]] used the Stealth Armor remotely in ''Hostile Takeover'' which later resulted in the suit's destruction.{{r|Iron Man: Armored Adventures Season 2 15}}

In ''Doomsday'', Pepper actually pilots the rebuilt Stealth Armor as opposed to remote-controlling it. She helps fend off chaos in [[New York City]] caused by portals appearing all over the world along with War Machine. Pepper proves to be a good pilot when out in the field.{{r|Iron Man: Armored Adventures Season 2 20}}

In ''The Dragonseed'', a cameo appearance was made, showing that it had been destroyed after Pepper's last piloted battle, which lead Tony to build Pepper her own suit of armor (the [[Stark Solutions X-51 Stealth Infiltrator Armor|Rescue Armor]]). This armor is basically re-colored and upgraded version of the Stealth Armor.{{r|Iron Man: Armored Adventures Season 2 24}}

| Properties              = 
*'''Superhuman Strength:''' It increases the wearer's strength to immense levels, allowing him to lift massive weights. It has later been upgraded for more strength for battle.
*'''Enhanced Durability:''' It is capable of amazing resilience and protection from harm. It's resilience has been upgraded to be more battle-worthy.
*'''Flight:''' It can hover and fly at incredible speeds through the use of boot jets.
*'''Repulsor Gauntlets:''' The gauntlets have many functions.
**'''Repulsors:''' Concussive force beams that are fired from the palms of the gauntlets.
**'''Force Field:''' They can project a force field that defends the user and others from harm.
**'''Sonic Cannons:''' It is equipped with sonic cannons to assault his opponents hearing.
*'''Unibeam:''' The armor's power source on the chest can emit a powerful concussive beam.
*'''Invisibility Function:''' The Stealth armor can become invisible to the human eye and undetectable to cameras and sensors, even those used by [[Stark International]]. The armor could even dampen the sound of his boot jet thrusters.
*'''Magnetic Manipulation:''' The armor can manipulate magnetism to repel metal objects.
*'''Hacking: '''It can use it hands to access doors to open.
*'''Flare Launchers:''' It can launch flares from the back.
*'''Power Usage''': It would appear the stealth capability severely drains its power over a short period of time, if using for a long time. He appears to have fixed this flaw when he upgraded the suit at the end of ''Titanium vs. Iron''.

}}
